sentences.zh: 儒林二

translations.literal: Confucian Scholars, Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian Scholars, Part Two

sentences.zh: ○胡旦賈同劉顏高弁孫復石介胡瑗劉羲叟林概李覯何涉王回

translations.literal: Hu Dan, Jia Tong, Liu Yan, Gao Bian, Sun Fu, Shi Jie, Hu Yuan, Liu Xisou, Lin Gai, Li Gou, He She, Wang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dan, Jia Tong, Liu Yan, Gao Bian, Sun Fu, Shi Jie, Hu Yuan, Liu Xisou, Lin Gai, Li Gou, He She, and Wang Hui

translations.literal: (younger brother Xiang).
translations.idiomatic: younger brother Xiang)

sentences.zh: 周堯卿王當陳暘

translations.literal: Zhou Yaoqing, Wang Dang, Chen Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yaoqing, Wang Dang, and Chen Yang

sentences.zh: 胡旦字周父，濱州渤海人。

translations.literal: Hu Dan, courtesy name Zhoufu, was a man of Bohai in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dan, courtesy name Zhoufu, was a native of Bohai in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少有雋才，博學能文辭。

translations.literal: From youth he had outstanding talent; he was broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he possessed outstanding talent; he was broadly learned and adept at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第一，為將作監丞、通判升州。

translations.literal: He placed first in the jinshi examination and was appointed Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and Vice Commissioner of Sheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He came in first on the jinshi examination and was appointed Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and Vice Commissioner of Sheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時江南初平，汰李氏時所度僧，十減六七。

translations.literal: At the time the Jiangnan region had just been pacified, and the monks ordained during the Li regime were reduced by six or seven tenths.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the south had just been pacified, and the monks ordained during the Li regime were cut by six or seven tenths.

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「彼無田廬可歸，將聚而為盜。」

translations.literal: Dan said, "They have no farmland or dwellings to return to; they will gather together and become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "They have no farms or homes to return to; they will gather together and become bandits."

sentences.zh: 悉黥為兵。

translations.literal: He tattooed them all as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He had them all tattooed and enrolled as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 遷左拾遺、直史館，數上書言時政利病。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Remonstrating Censor and Concurrent Academician of the Historical Records Office, and repeatedly submitted memorials on the advantages and disadvantages of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Remonstrating Censor and Concurrent Academician of the Historical Records Office, and repeatedly submitted memorials on the strengths and weaknesses of current policy.

sentences.zh: 出為淮南東路轉運副使、知海州。

translations.literal: He was dispatched as Vice Commissioner of the Huainan East Circuit Transport Service and Prefect of Ha Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Vice Commissioner of the Huainan East Circuit Transport Service and Prefect of Ha Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召歸。

translations.literal: After a year, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was summoned back.

sentences.zh: 先是，盧多遜貶，趙普罷相。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu Duosun had been demoted and Zhao Pu dismissed from the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lu Duosun had been demoted and Zhao Pu removed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 其夏，河決韓村，尋復塞。

translations.literal: That summer the Yellow River breached at Hancun, but was soon sealed again.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the Yellow River broke through at Hancun, but was soon blocked again.

sentences.zh: 旦獻《河平頌》曰：「天祚我宋，以君兆民。

translations.literal: Dan presented an "Ode on the Pacification of the River," saying, "Heaven has blessed our Song, to rule the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Dan presented an "Ode on the Pacification of the River," which began, "Heaven has blessed our Song, to rule the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 配天成休，惟堯與鄰。

translations.literal: Matching Heaven's gift of grace, we are peers only with Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Matching Heaven's grace, we stand only with Yao as a peer.

sentences.zh: 粵有大水，昏墊下人。

translations.literal: There arose a great flood that submerged and troubled the people below.
translations.idiomatic: A great flood arose, drowning the land and afflicting the people below.

sentences.zh: 非曰聖作，孰究孰度。

translations.literal: If it were not called the work of a sage, who could investigate and measure it?
translations.idiomatic: Were it not the work of a sage, who could investigate and reckon it?

sentences.zh: 蔽賢者退，壅澤者罪。

translations.literal: Those who blocked the worthy were removed; those who obstructed the waters were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who blocked worthy men were removed, and those who obstructed the waters were punished.

sentences.zh: 我防大患，河豈云敗。

translations.literal: We guarded against a great calamity; how could the river be said to have failed?
translations.idiomatic: We warded off a great disaster—how could the river be said to have been defeated?

sentences.zh: 逆遜遠投，奸普屏外。

translations.literal: The rebellious Duosun was sent far away; the scheming Pu was pushed outside the screen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebellious Duosun was cast far away, and the scheming Pu was driven beyond the court.

sentences.zh: 聖道如隄，崇崇海內。

translations.literal: The sage's way is like a dike, towering high throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's way is like a dike, rising high throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝曰守文，是塞是親。

translations.literal: The emperor is called one who preserves the written tradition; he both blocks and draws near.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is called a keeper of tradition; he both blocks the waters and draws close to his people.

sentences.zh: 調爾衛兵，程是烝民。

translations.literal: Deploy your guard soldiers; govern these common people.
translations.idiomatic: Muster your guard soldiers and govern the common people.

sentences.zh: 民以盡力，臣以勤職。

translations.literal: The people exert themselves fully; officials diligently perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: The people give their full strength, and officials diligently perform their duties.

sentences.zh: 役云其終，河以之塞。

translations.literal: When the labor was said to be finished, the river was sealed by it.
translations.idiomatic: When the labor was declared complete, the river was blocked by it.

sentences.zh: 唐堯懷山，實警神德。

translations.literal: Tang Yao's memory of mountains-in-flood truly warned of divine virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Yao remembered the mountains submerged in flood, it truly served as a warning of divine virtue.

sentences.zh: 漢武宣防，實彰令式。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han's declaration about blocking the waters truly displayed a model of good order.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Han proclaimed the blocking of the waters, it truly displayed a model of good governance.

sentences.zh: 我塞長河，融流惠澤。

translations.literal: We blocked the great river; its flowing waters spread beneficent grace.
translations.idiomatic: We blocked the great river, and its spreading waters brought beneficent grace.

sentences.zh: 明明聖功，萬代成則。」

translations.literal: Bright is the sage's achievement; for ten thousand generations it becomes a standard."
translations.idiomatic: Bright is the sage's achievement—it will serve as a standard for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 太宗覽頌有「逆遜、奸普」之語，召宰相謂曰：「胡旦獻頌，詞意悖戾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong read the ode and saw the phrases "rebellious Duosun" and "scheming Pu," he summoned the chancellors and said, "Hu Dan's submitted ode is rebellious and perverse in language and intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong read the ode and saw the phrases "rebellious Duosun" and "scheming Pu," he summoned the chancellors and said, "Hu Dan's submitted ode is perverse and insolent in both language and intent.

sentences.zh: 朕自擢於甲科，曆試外任，所至無善狀。

translations.literal: I myself promoted him from the top examination class and tested him in successive external appointments, yet everywhere he went he left no record of good conduct.
translations.idiomatic: I myself promoted him from the top examination class and tried him in successive posts outside the capital, yet everywhere he went he left no record of good service.

sentences.zh: 知海州日為部下所訟，猶已具，適會大赦，朕錄其材而舍其過，尚令在近列，又領史職，乃敢恣胸臆狂躁如此，其亟逐之！」

translations.literal: When he was Prefect of Ha Prefecture his subordinates sued him, and the case was already complete; it happened to coincide with a general amnesty. I valued his talent and overlooked his faults, yet still kept him in the near ranks and also entrusted him with historical duties—and now he dares to indulge his breast and act so wildly and rashly. Expel him at once!"
translations.idiomatic: When he served as Prefect of Ha Prefecture his subordinates brought suit against him, and the case was already complete; it happened to coincide with a general amnesty. I valued his talent and overlooked his faults, yet still kept him in the inner ranks and also entrusted him with historical duties—and now he dares to give free rein to such wild and reckless presumption. Expel him at once!"

sentences.zh: 即貶殿中丞、商州團練副使。

translations.literal: He was immediately demoted to Palace Director and Vice Commissioner of the Shangzhou Military Training Corps.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately demoted to Palace Director and Vice Commissioner of the Shangzhou Military Training Corps.

sentences.zh: 上《平燕議》曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a "Plan for Pacifying Yan," saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a "Plan for Pacifying Yan," which stated:

sentences.zh: 今幽州在北門之外，東封非國家所急，願移其資以事北伐。

translations.literal: You Prefecture now lies beyond the northern gate; the eastern feng ceremony is not urgent for the state. I wish to shift those resources to the business of a northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: You Prefecture now lies beyond the northern gate, and the eastern feng ceremony is not an urgent national priority. I wish to redirect those resources toward a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 且天時、地利、人事皆有可伐之意。

translations.literal: Moreover, in celestial timing, geographical advantage, and human affairs alike there are signs that favor an attack.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in celestial timing, geographical advantage, and human affairs alike, all signs point toward an attack.

sentences.zh: 歲之所臨，其地受福。

translations.literal: Where the year's star stands, that region receives blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the year's star stands, that region receives its blessing.

sentences.zh: 今年春末至來年，歲在宋分，今年初秋至六年，鎮在燕分。

translations.literal: From late spring this year until next year the year star will be in Song's quarter; from early autumn this year until year six the quarter star will be in Yan's quarter.
translations.idiomatic: From late spring this year until next year the year star will favor Song territory; from early autumn this year until the sixth year the quarter star will favor Yan territory.

sentences.zh: 從今年為備，至來春興師。

translations.literal: Begin preparations from this year and launch the army next spring.
translations.idiomatic: Begin preparations this year and launch the campaign next spring.

sentences.zh: 北兵之遇春夏，則氈裘、皮履、羊弓、塞馬不為用，而中原士卒素不能寒，往北逢暄，筋力勇健。

translations.literal: When northern armies encounter spring and summer, felt garments, leather boots, composite bows, and frontier horses are of no use, whereas Central Plains soldiers are by nature unused to cold; going north when the weather turns warm, their sinews and strength become vigorous and bold.
translations.idiomatic: When northern armies encounter spring and summer, felt garments, leather boots, composite bows, and frontier horses are of little use, whereas Central Plains soldiers are unused to cold by nature; marching north when the weather turns warm, their sinews grow vigorous and their strength bold.

sentences.zh: 以勇健之士驅不用之敵，承福慶之時討災殃之城，成功立事，在於此矣。

translations.literal: Driving vigorous troops against enemies whose equipment is useless, at a time of auspicious fortune attacking a city suffering calamity—success and achievement lie in this.
translations.idiomatic: To drive vigorous troops against enemies whose equipment is ill-suited to the season, and at a time of auspicious fortune to attack a city stricken by calamity—success and achievement lie in this.

sentences.zh: 長淮以北，太行以東，河水罷災，土地甚沃。

translations.literal: North of the Long Huai and east of the Taihang Mountains, the river's flood disaster had ceased and the land was very fertile.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Huai River and east of the Taihang Mountains, the river's flood damage had ceased and the land was very fertile.

sentences.zh: 因其豐實，取其穀帛，減價以折納，見錢以貴糴，官府多積，兵役無虞，用兵豐財，可濟大事。

translations.literal: Drawing on this abundance, collect its grain and cloth; cut prices for corvée conversion payments and use cash to buy grain at premium rates. With government stores greatly accumulated and military provisions secure, deploying troops with ample funds can support a great undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on this abundance, collect grain and cloth; reduce prices for corvée conversion payments and use cash to buy grain at premium rates. With government stores greatly accumulated and military provisions secure, a campaign financed with ample resources can support a great undertaking.

sentences.zh: 太原克復以來，於今七載，兵甲甚利，士卒甚雄，夜寢晨興，寒裘饑粟。

translations.literal: Seven years have passed since Taiyuan was recovered; weapons and armor are very sharp, soldiers very stalwart, sleeping at night and rising at dawn in cold furs and on meager grain.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years have passed since Taiyuan was recovered; weapons and armor are very sharp, soldiers very stalwart, sleeping at night and rising at dawn in cold furs and on meager rations.

sentences.zh: 若以促裝之賜，發軍而用之，恩賞之貲，成功而賚之，可以齊心平敵，恢拓舊境。

translations.literal: If emergency outfitting allowances are used to mobilize the army, and bounty rewards granted upon success, hearts can be united, enemies leveled, and old territory recovered and expanded.
translations.idiomatic: If emergency outfitting allowances are used to mobilize the army and bounty rewards granted upon success, hearts can be united, enemies overcome, and old territory recovered and expanded.

sentences.zh: 幽州平土而負敵，為勢必擇四人，分之方面，以剛斷勇毅者主之，選和平恭慎者一人部之。

translations.literal: You Prefecture lies on flat land and borders the enemy; given the situation one must choose four men and divide the directions among them, with resolute and bold commanders in charge, and select one peaceful and cautious man to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: You Prefecture lies on flat terrain and borders the enemy; given the situation one must choose four commanders and assign each a direction, with resolute and bold men in charge, and select one peaceful and cautious official to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 幽州之北，皆是山谷，通人馬者不過十處，領將士者亦擇十人，同行則共議兵機，分出則各司軍事，寇來則同戰以驅逐，寇歸則畫疆以扞蔽。

translations.literal: North of You Prefecture are all valleys; places passable by men and horses number no more than ten. Choose ten commanders as well: when traveling together they jointly discuss military strategy; when separated each manages his own troops. When invaders come they fight together to drive them off; when invaders withdraw they draw boundaries to block and shield.
translations.idiomatic: North of You Prefecture lie nothing but valleys; places passable by men and horses number no more than ten. Choose ten commanders as well: when traveling together they jointly discuss military strategy, and when separated each manages his own troops. When invaders come they fight together to drive them off; when invaders withdraw they draw boundaries to block and shield.

sentences.zh: 苟塞斷山路，餘寇在燕與大軍相持，則遷延其時以度春夏，寇不能熱，有退無前。

translations.literal: If mountain routes are blocked and cut off, and remaining invaders in Yan hold out against the main army, then prolong the time to pass through spring and summer; the invaders cannot endure the heat and will retreat without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: If mountain routes are blocked and cut off, and remaining invaders in Yan hold out against the main army, then prolong the engagement through spring and summer; the invaders cannot endure the heat and will retreat without advancing.

sentences.zh: 使士之剛勇才力者各為一將，多則分部扞敵攻城，兩盡其力。

translations.literal: Let the most resolute, brave, and talented soldiers each serve as a general; when numerous, divide forces to block the enemy and besiege cities, deploying both sides' strength to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Let the most resolute, brave, and talented soldiers each serve as a general; when forces are numerous, divide them to block the enemy and besiege cities, deploying both sides' strength to the full.

sentences.zh: 定其軍名，實其軍數。

translations.literal: Fix their army names and make their troop counts accurate.
translations.idiomatic: Establish formal army names and accurate troop counts.

sentences.zh: 我寡彼多則力不勝，我實彼虛則勝有餘。

translations.literal: If we are few and they many, strength cannot prevail; if we are real and they empty, victory will be more than sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: If we are few and they many, strength cannot prevail; if our numbers are real and theirs inflated, victory will be more than sufficient.

sentences.zh: 力均則較其地形，地均則爭其謀略，分明勇怯，各致其用。

translations.literal: When strength is equal, compare terrain; when terrain is equal, contest strategy; distinguish courage from cowardice and employ each to full effect.
translations.idiomatic: When strength is equal, compare terrain; when terrain is equal, contest strategy; distinguish the courageous from the timid and employ each to full effect.

sentences.zh: 以茶鹽香藥之價十分減二，從新者先賣於邊城要路、軍馬屯所。

translations.literal: Reduce the prices of tea, salt, and aromatics by two tenths, and sell the newest goods first at border strongpoints, key routes, and military encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the prices of tea, salt, and aromatics by twenty percent, and sell the newest goods first at border strongpoints, key routes, and military encampments.

sentences.zh: 以芻粟錢帛之價十分增二，納貨以出券者詣本場以交貨，得貨者緣逐路以納稅。

translations.literal: Raise the prices of fodder, grain, and cloth by two tenths; those who pay goods and receive certificates go to the depot to collect goods, and those who obtain goods pay taxes along their route.
translations.idiomatic: Raise the prices of fodder, grain, and cloth by twenty percent; those who pay goods and receive certificates go to the depot to collect goods, and those who obtain goods pay taxes along their route.

sentences.zh: 出往來四方之饒，為兩地費用之耗，自然商得其利，則買之於人，人得其資，則勤之於穡。

translations.literal: Release the abundance circulating in all four directions as the cost of cross-territory expenses; naturally merchants will gain profit and buy from the people, and the people will gain resources and work diligently at farming.
translations.idiomatic: Release the abundance circulating throughout the realm as the cost of cross-territory exchange; naturally merchants will gain profit and buy from the people, and the people will gain income and work diligently at farming.

sentences.zh: 故必民效兼倍之力，國貯九年之積，科撥不假於度支，轉般何勞於漕挽。

translations.literal: Thus the people will surely exert redoubled effort, the state will store up nine years' accumulation, appropriations will not depend on the Revenue Bureau, and transport convoys will not need to toil at canal hauling.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the people will surely exert redoubled effort, the state will store up nine years' grain, appropriations will not depend on the Revenue Bureau, and transport convoys will not need to toil at canal hauling.

sentences.zh: 芻粟之給，攻具之用，委輸發運，以為後繼。

translations.literal: Supplies of fodder and grain and the use of siege equipment shall be delivered and transported as follow-up reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies of fodder and grain and the use of siege equipment shall be delivered and transported as follow-up reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 今將用二十萬之眾，役三十州之民，願陛下明降日月之信，先示雨露之澤。

translations.literal: Now about to employ an army of two hundred thousand and conscript the people of thirty prefectures, I wish Your Majesty clearly to announce pledges as bright as the sun and moon, and first display grace like rain and dew.
translations.idiomatic: We are about to mobilize an army of two hundred thousand and conscript the people of thirty prefectures. I wish Your Majesty clearly to announce pledges as steadfast as the sun and moon, and first bestow grace like rain and dew.

sentences.zh: 民知信賞則悅而忘死，士得仰給則死而力戰。

translations.literal: When the people know rewards are trustworthy they will rejoice and forget death; when soldiers receive provisions they will die fighting with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: When the people know rewards are trustworthy they will gladly face death; when soldiers receive provisions they will fight to the death with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 如此則逆壘不足下，猾寇不足殄也。

translations.literal: In this way the rebel stronghold cannot fail to fall, and the cunning enemy cannot fail to be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the rebel stronghold cannot fail to fall, and the cunning enemy cannot fail to be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 起為左補闕，復直史館。

translations.literal: He was reappointed Left Supple Censor and again served concurrently in the Historical Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed Left Supple Censor and again served concurrently in the Historical Records Office.

sentences.zh: 遷修撰，預修國史，以尚書戶部員外郎知制誥，遷司封員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler, participated in compiling the National History, was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue with drafting authority, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler, participated in compiling the National History, was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue with drafting authority, and was then promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 有傭書人翟穎者，旦嘗與之善，因為改姓名馬周，以為唐馬周復出，上書詆時政，且自薦可為大臣。

translations.literal: There was a copyist named Zhai Ying with whom Dan had once been on good terms; he had him change his name to Ma Zhou, as though the Tang Ma Zhou had reappeared, and submit a memorial slandering current policy while also recommending himself as fit to serve as a high minister.
translations.idiomatic: There was a copyist named Zhai Ying with whom Dan had once been on good terms; Dan had him change his name to Ma Zhou, as though the Tang official Ma Zhou had reappeared, and submit a memorial criticizing current policy while also recommending himself as fit to serve as a high minister.

sentences.zh: 又舉材任輔者十人，其辭頗壯。

translations.literal: He also recommended ten men of talent suitable to serve as assistants; the language was quite bold.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended ten men of talent suitable to serve as assistants, and the language was notably bold.

sentences.zh: 當時皆謂旦所為。

translations.literal: At the time all believed Dan was behind it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone believed Dan was behind it.

sentences.zh: 馬周坐流海島，旦亦貶坊州團練副使。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou was exiled to a maritime island for his offense, and Dan was also demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Fangzhou Military Training Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou was exiled to a maritime island for his offense, and Dan was also demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Fangzhou Military Training Corps.

sentences.zh: 坐擅離所部謁宋白於鄜州，既被劾，特釋之。

translations.literal: He was prosecuted for leaving his post without authorization to visit Song Bai at Fuzhou; though impeached, he was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was prosecuted for leaving his post without authorization to visit Song Bai at Fuzhou; though impeached, he was specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 徙絳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 稍復工部員外郎、直集賢院，遷本曹郎中、知制誥、史館修撰。

translations.literal: He was gradually restored to Vice Director of the Works Department and Concurrent Academician of the Hall of Worthies, then promoted to Director of that bureau with drafting authority and Historical Records compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually restored to Vice Director of the Works Department and Concurrent Academician of the Hall of Worthies, then promoted to Director of that bureau with drafting authority and Historical Records compilation.

sentences.zh: 素善中官王繼恩，為繼恩草制辭過美。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with the eunuch Wang Jien and drafted appointment documents for him with excessive praise.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with the eunuch Wang Jien and drafted appointment documents for him with excessive praise.

sentences.zh: 繼恩敗，真宗聞而惡之，貶安遠軍行軍司馬，又削籍流潯州。

translations.literal: When Wang Jien fell, Emperor Zhenzong heard of it and despised him; he was demoted to Army Marshal of Anyuan and later stripped of his registry and exiled to Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jien fell, Emperor Zhenzong learned of this and despised him; he was demoted to Army Marshal of Anyuan and later stripped of his registry and exiled to Xun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，移通州團練副使，徙徐州，以祠部員外郎分司西京，又為保信軍節度副使。

translations.literal: In the early Xianping era he was moved to Vice Commissioner of the Tong Prefecture Military Training Corps, then transferred to Xu Prefecture, served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites at the Western Capital branch office, and was again appointed Vice Military Commissioner of Baoxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianping era he was moved to Vice Commissioner of the Tong Prefecture Military Training Corps, then transferred to Xu Prefecture, served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites at the Western Capital branch office, and was again appointed Vice Military Commissioner of Baoxin.

sentences.zh: 久之，以司封員外郎通判襄州。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites as Vice Commissioner of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites as Vice Commissioner of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，改祠部郎中，服母喪，既除，乃言父卒時嘗詔奪哀從事，請追行服三年。

translations.literal: During the Mount Tai feng ceremony he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Rites; after completing mourning for his mother and resuming office, he stated that when his father died he had been ordered by edict to set aside mourning and continue service, and requested to observe three years of mourning retroactively.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mount Tai feng ceremony he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Rites. After completing mourning for his mother and resuming office, he stated that when his father died he had been ordered by edict to set aside mourning and continue service, and requested to observe three years of mourning retroactively.

sentences.zh: 已而失明，以秘書省少監致仕，居襄州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went blind, retired as Vice Director of the Secretariat, and resided in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went blind, retired as Vice Director of the Secretariat, and lived in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 再遷秘書監，卒。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Director of the Secretariat, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was twice promoted to Director of the Secretariat, then died.

sentences.zh: 旦喜讀書，既喪明，猶令人誦經史，隱幾聽之不少輟。

translations.literal: Dan loved reading; even after losing his sight he still had others recite the classics and histories to him, listening while reclining on a couch without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Dan loved reading; even after losing his sight he still had others recite the classics and histories to him, listening without pause while reclining on a couch.

sentences.zh: 著《漢春秋》、《五代史略》、《將帥要略》、《演聖通論》、《唐乘》、《家傳》三百餘卷。

translations.literal: He authored more than three hundred chapters, including Han Spring and Autumn, Brief History of the Five Dynasties, Essentials for Generals and Commanders, Comprehensive Discussion of the Sage's Teaching, Tang Dynasty Records, and Family Biographies.
translations.idiomatic: He authored more than three hundred chapters, including Han Spring and Autumn, Brief History of the Five Dynasties, Essentials for Generals and Commanders, Comprehensive Discussion of the Sage's Teaching, Tang Dynasty Records, and Family Biographies.

sentences.zh: 斫大硯，方五六尺，刻而瘞之，曰「胡旦修《漢春秋》硯。」

translations.literal: He carved a large inkstone five or six chi square, inscribed it, and buried it, saying, "Hu Dan's inkstone for compiling Han Spring and Autumn."
translations.idiomatic: He carved a large inkstone five or six chi square, inscribed it, and buried it, labeling it "Hu Dan's Inkstone for Compiling Han Spring and Autumn."

sentences.zh: 晚尤黷貨，干擾州縣，持吏短長，為時論所薄。

translations.literal: In his later years he was especially greedy for wealth, interfering in prefecture and county affairs and wielding officials' flaws against them; contemporary opinion held him in low regard.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was especially greedy for wealth, interfering in prefecture and county affairs and wielding officials' flaws against them, and contemporary opinion held him in low regard.

sentences.zh: 既死，子孫貧甚，寓柩民間。

translations.literal: After his death his descendants were extremely poor and housed his coffin among common people.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his descendants were destitute and kept his coffin lodged among common households.

sentences.zh: 皇祐末，知襄州王田為言於朝，得錢二十萬以葬。

translations.literal: In the late Huangyou era, Wang Tian, Prefect of Xiang Prefecture, spoke on his behalf to the court and obtained two hundred thousand cash for burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Huangyou era, Wang Tian, Prefect of Xiang Prefecture, petitioned the court on his behalf and obtained two hundred thousand cash for burial.

sentences.zh: 賈同字希得，青州臨淄人。

translations.literal: Jia Tong, courtesy name Xide, was a man of Linzi in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Tong, courtesy name Xide, was a native of Linzi in Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五代時，楊光遠反，同祖崇率鄉里四百餘家保愚穀山，全活者二千人。

translations.literal: During the Five Dynasties, when Yang Guangyuan rebelled, Tong's grandfather Chong led more than four hundred local families to hold Mount Yugu, saving two thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties, when Yang Guangyuan rebelled, Tong's grandfather Chong led more than four hundred local families to hold Mount Yugu, saving two thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 同初名罔，字公疏，篤學好古，有時名，著《山東野錄》七篇。

translations.literal: Tong's original name was Wang, courtesy name Gongshu; he was devoted to learning and loved antiquity, enjoyed contemporary renown, and wrote seven chapters of Records from the Eastern Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's original name was Wang, courtesy name Gongshu; he was devoted to learning and loved antiquity, enjoyed contemporary renown, and wrote seven chapters of Records from the Eastern Mountains.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，同進士出身，真宗命改今名。

translations.literal: After forty he passed the jinshi examination; Emperor Zhenzong ordered him to adopt his present name.
translations.idiomatic: After passing forty he obtained jinshi status; Emperor Zhenzong ordered him to adopt his present name.

sentences.zh: 王欽若方貴盛，聞同名，欲致之，固謝不往。

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo was at the height of power; hearing of someone with the same name, he wished to summon him, but Tong firmly declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo was at the height of power; hearing of someone with the same name, he wished to summon him, but Tong firmly declined and did not go.

sentences.zh: 居八九年，始補曆城主簿。

translations.literal: After eight or nine years he was finally appointed Clerk of Licheng County.
translations.idiomatic: After eight or nine years he was finally appointed clerk of Licheng County.

sentences.zh: 張知白薦為大理評事，通判兗州。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhibai recommended him as Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review and Vice Commissioner of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhibai recommended him as Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review and Vice Commissioner of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，上書言：「自祥符以來，諫諍路塞，丁謂乘間造符瑞以欺先帝。

translations.literal: In the early Tiansheng era he submitted a memorial saying, "Since the Xiangfu era the path for remonstrance has been blocked; Ding Wei seized the opportunity to fabricate auspicious omens to deceive the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tiansheng era he submitted a memorial stating, "Since the Xiangfu era the path for remonstrance has been blocked; Ding Wei seized the opportunity to fabricate auspicious omens to deceive the former emperor.

sentences.zh: 今謂奸既白，宜明告天下，正符瑞之謬，罷宮觀崇奉，歸不急之衛兵，收無名之實費，使先帝免後世之議，國家無因循之失。」

translations.literal: Now that Wei's treachery has been exposed, the court should clearly announce to all under heaven the falsity of auspicious omens, abolish lavish support of palace temples, return unnecessary guard soldiers, and recover useless expenditures, so that the former emperor may be spared later criticism and the state may avoid continuing error."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Wei's treachery has been exposed, the court should clearly announce to all under heaven the falsity of auspicious omens, abolish lavish support of palace temples, return unnecessary guard soldiers, and recover useless expenditures, so that the former emperor may be spared later criticism and the state may avoid continuing error."

sentences.zh: 又言：「寇準忠規亮節，疾惡擯邪。

translations.literal: He also said, "Kou Zhun's loyal counsel and bright integrity, his hatred of evil and rejection of wickedness—
translations.idiomatic: He also stated, "Kou Zhun's loyal counsel and bright integrity, his hatred of evil and rejection of wickedness—

sentences.zh: 自其貶黜，天下之人弗見其罪，宜還之內地，以明忠邪善惡之分。」

translations.literal: Since his demotion the people under heaven have not seen his crimes; he should be recalled to the interior to clarify the distinction between loyalty and treachery, good and evil."
translations.idiomatic: Since his demotion the people under heaven have not seen his crimes; he should be recalled to the interior to clarify the distinction between loyalty and treachery, good and evil."

sentences.zh: 時章獻太后臨朝，而同言如此，人以為難。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhangxian was regent at the time, yet Tong spoke so; people considered it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhangxian was regent at the time, yet Tong spoke so boldly that people admired his courage.

sentences.zh: 再遷殿中丞、知棣州，卒。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Palace Director and Prefect of Di Prefecture, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Palace Director and Prefect of Di Prefecture, then died.

sentences.zh: 劉顏、李冠、王無忌及其門人諡同曰存道先生。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, Li Guan, Wang Wuji, and his disciples posthumously honored Tong with the title Master Cundao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, Li Guan, Wang Wuji, and his disciples posthumously honored Tong with the title Master Cundao.

sentences.zh: 劉顏字子望，彭城人。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, courtesy name Ziwang, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, courtesy name Ziwang, was a native of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 少孤，好古，學不專章句。

translations.literal: From youth he was orphaned; he loved antiquity and did not specialize in commentarial glosses.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he loved antiquity and did not limit his study to commentarial glosses.

sentences.zh: 師事高弁。

translations.literal: He took Gao Bian as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Gao Bian.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第，以試秘書省校書郎知龍興縣，坐法免。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and, through examination, was appointed Proofreader of the Secretariat and Prefect of Longxing County; he was dismissed for violation of law.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and, through examination, was appointed Proofreader of the Secretariat and Prefect of Longxing County; he was dismissed for a legal offense.

sentences.zh: 久之，授徐州文學。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Literary Instructor of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Literary Instructor of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 居鄉里，教授數十百人。

translations.literal: Living in his home district, he instructed several hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: Living in his home district, he instructed several hundred students.

sentences.zh: 采漢、唐奏議為《輔弼名對》。

translations.literal: He collected Han and Tang memorials into Notable Exchanges of Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: He collected Han and Tang memorials into Notable Exchanges of Assistants.

sentences.zh: 馮元、劉筠、錢易、滕涉、蔡齊上其書，除任城主簿。

translations.literal: Feng Yuan, Liu Jun, Qian Yi, Teng She, and Cai Qi submitted his book; he was appointed Clerk of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yuan, Liu Jun, Qian Yi, Teng She, and Cai Qi submitted his book to the court, and he was appointed clerk of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發大姓所積粟，活數千人。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he opened the grain stored by great clans and saved several thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he opened the grain stored by great clans and saved several thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 李迪知兗州、青州，皆辟為從事，卒。

translations.literal: When Li Di was Prefect of Yan and Qing prefectures, he recruited him as staff in both cases; he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Di served as Prefect of Yan and Qing prefectures, he recruited Yan as staff in both posts; Yan later died.

sentences.zh: 著《儒術通要》、《經濟樞言》復數十篇。

translations.literal: He authored several dozen chapters including Essentials of Confucian Technique and Key Points on State Economy.
translations.idiomatic: He authored several dozen chapters, including Essentials of Confucian Technique and Key Points on State Economy.

sentences.zh: 石介見其書，歎曰：「恨不在弟子之列。」

translations.literal: Shi Jie saw his books and sighed, saying, "I regret not being among his disciples."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jie read his books and sighed, "I regret not being among his disciples."

sentences.zh: 子庠，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Kuang has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuang has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 高弁字公儀，濮州雷澤人。

translations.literal: Gao Bian, courtesy name Gongyi, was a man of Leize in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bian, courtesy name Gongyi, was a native of Leize in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，徒步從種放學於終南山，又學古文於柳開，與張景齊名。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he traveled on foot to study with Zhong Fang on Zhongnan Mountain, and also studied ancient prose with Liu Kai, becoming as famous as Zhang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he traveled on foot to study with Zhong Fang on Zhongnan Mountain, and also studied ancient prose with Liu Kai, becoming as renowned as Zhang Jing.

sentences.zh: 至道中，以文謁王禹偁，禹偁奇之。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era he presented literary works to Wang Yucheng, who was impressed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao era he presented literary works to Wang Yucheng, who was greatly impressed.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累官侍御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through successive posts to Censor-in-Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through successive posts to Censor-in-Attendant.

sentences.zh: 諫修玉清昭應宮，降知廣濟軍。

translations.literal: He remonstrated against constructing the Jade Clarity Zhaoying Palace and was demoted to Prefect of Guangji Army.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated against constructing the Jade Clarity Zhaoying Palace and was demoted to Prefect of Guangji Army.

sentences.zh: 尋以戶部判官試開封府進士，私發糊名，奪二官。

translations.literal: Soon, while serving as an examiner of Kaifeng jinshi candidates with the Ministry of Revenue, he privately opened sealed names and had two ranks stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, while serving as an examiner of Kaifeng jinshi candidates with the Ministry of Revenue, he privately opened sealed names and was stripped of two ranks.

sentences.zh: 稍復知單州、邢州、鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He was gradually restored to Prefect of Dan and Xing prefectures and Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually restored to Prefect of Dan and Xing prefectures and Commissioner of Salt and Iron.

sentences.zh: 河決澶州，請弛堤防，縱水所之，可省民力，且以扼契丹南向。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River breached at D Prefecture, he requested relaxing the dikes and letting the water go where it would, which could save the people's labor and also block the Khitan from moving south.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River breached at D Prefecture, he requested relaxing the dikes and letting the water go where it would, which could spare the people's labor and also block the Khitan from moving south.

sentences.zh: 議寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 知陝州，卒。

translations.literal: He became Prefect of Shan Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Prefect of Shan Prefecture, then died.

sentences.zh: 弁性孝友。

translations.literal: Bian was by nature filial and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was by nature filial and fraternal.

sentences.zh: 所為文章多祖《六經》及《孟子》，喜言仁義。

translations.literal: The writings he produced mostly took the Six Classics and Mencius as models, and he delighted in speaking of benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His writings mostly took the Six Classics and Mencius as models, and he delighted in speaking of benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 有《帝則》三篇，為世所傳。

translations.literal: He had three chapters of Imperial Norms, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote three chapters of Imperial Norms, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 與李迪、賈同、陸參、朱頔、伊淳相友善。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Li Di, Jia Tong, Lu Can, Zhu Di, and Yi Chun.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Li Di, Jia Tong, Lu Can, Zhu Di, and Yi Chun.

sentences.zh: 石延年、劉潛皆其門人也。

translations.literal: Shi Yannian and Liu Qian were both his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yannian and Liu Qian were both his disciples.

sentences.zh: 孫復，字明復，晉州平陽人。

translations.literal: Sun Fu, courtesy name Mingfu, was a man of Pingyang in Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu, courtesy name Mingfu, was a native of Pingyang in Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士不第，退居泰山。

translations.literal: He failed the jinshi examination and retired to Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi examination and retired to Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 學《春秋》，著《尊王發微》十二篇，大約本於陸淳，而增新意。

translations.literal: He studied Spring and Autumn Annals and wrote twelve chapters of Honoring the King and Revealing Subtleties, generally based on Lu Chun but adding new ideas.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Spring and Autumn Annals and wrote twelve chapters of Honoring the King and Revealing Subtleties, generally based on Lu Chun but adding new ideas of his own.

sentences.zh: 石介有名山東，自介而下皆以先生事復。

translations.literal: Shi Jie was famous in Shandong; from Jie downward all treated Fu as their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jie was famous in Shandong; from Jie downward all treated Fu as their master.

sentences.zh: 年四十不娶。

translations.literal: He did not marry until forty.
translations.idiomatic: He had not married by the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 李迪知其賢，以其弟之子妻之。

translations.literal: Li Di knowing his virtue gave him his younger brother's son as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Li Di, recognizing his virtue, gave him his younger brother's son in marriage.

sentences.zh: 復初猶豫，石介與諸弟子請曰：「公卿不下士久矣，今丞相不以先生貧賤，欲托以子，宜因以成丞相之賢名。」

translations.literal: Fu initially hesitated; Shi Jie and the disciples pleaded, saying, "Nobles and ministers have not deigned to employ scholars for a long time; now the chief minister, not considering the Master's poverty and low status, wishes to entrust his son to you—you should accept thereby to complete the chief minister's reputation for virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Fu initially hesitated, but Shi Jie and the other disciples pleaded, "Nobles and ministers have not deigned to employ scholars for a long time. Now the chief minister, not considering the Master's poverty and low status, wishes to entrust his son to you—you should accept and thereby complete the chief minister's reputation for virtue."

sentences.zh: 復乃聽。

translations.literal: Fu then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Fu then consented.

sentences.zh: 孔道輔聞復之賢，就見之，介執杖屨立侍復左右，升降拜則扶之，其往謝亦然。

translations.literal: Kong Daofu hearing of Fu's virtue came to visit him; Jie holding staff and shoes stood attending Fu's side, and when Fu rose, descended, or bowed he would support him—the same when going to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Daofu, hearing of Fu's virtue, came to visit him. Jie held staff and shoes and stood attending Fu's side; when Fu rose, descended, or bowed, Jie would support him, and did the same when going to thank Daofu.

sentences.zh: 介既為學官，語人曰：「孫先生非隱者也。」

translations.literal: After Jie became instructor, he told people, "Master Sun is no recluse."
translations.idiomatic: After Jie became an instructor, he told people, "Master Sun is no recluse."

sentences.zh: 於是范仲淹、富弼皆言復有經術，宜在朝廷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi both said Fu had classical learning and should be in court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi both said that Fu possessed classical learning and should serve at court.

sentences.zh: 除秘書省校書郎、國子監直講。

translations.literal: He was appointed Proofreader of the Secretariat and Instructor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Proofreader of the Secretariat and Instructor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸太學，賜緋衣銀魚，召為邇英閣祗候說書。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the Imperial Academy, he was granted a red robe and silver fish badge and summoned as Lecturer for the Court of Immediate Favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage visited the Imperial Academy, he was granted a red robe and silver fish badge and summoned as Lecturer for the Court of Immediate Favor.

sentences.zh: 楊安國言其講說多異先儒，罷之。

translations.literal: Yang Anguo said his lectures differed greatly from earlier Confucians, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Anguo said his lectures differed greatly from earlier Confucians, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 孔直溫敗，得所遺復詩，坐貶虔州監稅，徙泗州，又知長水縣，簽書應天府判官事。

translations.literal: When Kong Zhiwen was defeated, poems Fu had sent him were found; Fu was demoted to Tax Supervisor of Qian Prefecture, transferred to Si Prefecture, then appointed Prefect of Changshui County and Signing Assistant Judge of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Zhiwen fell, poems Fu had sent him were discovered; Fu was demoted to Tax Supervisor of Qian Prefecture, transferred to Si Prefecture, then appointed Prefect of Changshui County and Signing Assistant Judge of Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 通判陵州，未行，翰林學士趙概等十餘人言復經為人師，不宜使佐州縣。

translations.literal: As Vice Commissioner of Ling Prefecture, before taking up his post, Hanlin Academician Zhao Gai and more than ten others said Fu had long been a teacher of men and should not be made to assist prefecture and county.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Vice Commissioner of Ling Prefecture, he had not yet departed when Hanlin Academician Zhao Gai and more than ten others stated that Fu had long been a teacher of men and should not be made to assist prefecture and county administration.

sentences.zh: 留為直講，稍遷殿中丞，卒，賜錢十萬。

translations.literal: He was retained as Instructor, gradually promoted to Palace Director, then died; he was granted one hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was retained as Instructor, gradually promoted to Palace Director, then died; the court granted one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 復與胡瑗不合，在太學常相避。

translations.literal: Fu and Hu Yuan did not get along; in the Imperial Academy they often avoided each other.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Hu Yuan did not get along; in the Imperial Academy they often avoided each other.

sentences.zh: 瑗治經不如復，而教養諸生過之。

translations.literal: Yuan's mastery of the classics was not equal to Fu's, but his nurture and teaching of students surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's mastery of the classics was not equal to Fu's, but his nurture and teaching of students surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 復既病，韓琦言於仁宗，選書吏，給紙筆，命其門人祖無擇就復家得書十五萬言，錄藏秘閣。

translations.literal: When Fu fell ill, Han Qi spoke to Renzong, selected clerks, supplied paper and brush, and ordered his disciple Zu Wujue to go to Fu's home and obtain one hundred fifty thousand characters of writing, which were copied and stored in the Secret Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu fell ill, Han Qi spoke to Emperor Renzong, selected clerks, supplied paper and brush, and ordered his disciple Zu Wujue to go to Fu's home and obtain one hundred fifty thousand characters of writing, which were copied and stored in the Secret Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 特官其一子。

translations.literal: One of his sons was specially granted official rank.
translations.idiomatic: One of his sons was specially granted official rank.

sentences.zh: 石介，字守道，兗州奉符人。

translations.literal: Shi Jie, courtesy name Shoudao, was a man of Fengfu in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jie, courtesy name Shoudao, was a native of Fengfu in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，曆鄆州、南京推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and successively served as judicial officer of Yan and Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and successively served as judicial officer of Yan and Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 篤學有誌尚，樂善疾惡，喜聲名，遇事奮然敢為。

translations.literal: Devoted to learning with aspiration, he loved the good and hated evil, delighted in renown, and when encountering affairs acted boldly and daringly.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to learning and possessed of high aspiration, he loved the good and hated evil, delighted in renown, and when encountering affairs acted boldly and daringly.

sentences.zh: 御史臺辟為主簿，未至，以論赦書不當求五代及諸偽國後，罷為鎮南掌書記。

translations.literal: The Censorate recruited him as clerk, but before he arrived, because he argued that the amnesty edict should not seek descendants of the Five Dynasties and various puppet states, he was dismissed and became secretary of Zhennan.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate recruited him as clerk, but before he arrived, because he argued that the amnesty edict should not seek descendants of the Five Dynasties and various puppet states, he was dismissed and became secretary of Zhennan.

sentences.zh: 代父丙遠官，為嘉州軍事判官。

translations.literal: He replaced his father Bing in distant office and became military judge of Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced his father Bing in distant office and became military judge of Jia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁父母憂，耕徂徠山下，葬五世之未葬者七十喪。

translations.literal: During mourning for his parents, he farmed below Mount Culai and buried seventy unburied corpses of five generations.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his parents, he farmed below Mount Culai and buried seventy unburied corpses spanning five generations.

sentences.zh: 以《易》教授於家，魯人號介徂徠先生。

translations.literal: He taught the Changes at home; people of Lu called him Master Culai of Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the Changes at home, and people of Lu called him Master Culai of Jie.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監直講，學者從之甚眾，太學繇此益盛。

translations.literal: He entered as Instructor of the Imperial Academy; many students followed him, and the Imperial Academy thereby grew more flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Instructor of the Imperial Academy; many students followed him, and the Imperial Academy thereby grew more flourishing.

sentences.zh: 介為文有氣，嘗患文章之弊，佛、老為蠹，著《怪說》、《中國論》，言去此三者，乃可以有為。

translations.literal: Jie's writing had vigor; he once lamented the disease of literature—that Buddhist and Daoist teachings were pests; he wrote On the Strange and On China, saying that removing these three things one could then achieve things.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's writing had vigor. He once lamented the disease of literature—that Buddhist and Daoist teachings were pests—and wrote On the Strange and On China, arguing that only by removing these three things could the state truly act.

sentences.zh: 又著《唐鑒》以戒奸臣、宦官、宮女，指切當時，無所諱忌。

translations.literal: He also wrote Mirror of Tang to warn against treacherous ministers, eunuchs, and palace women, pointing at the present without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Mirror of Tang to warn against treacherous ministers, eunuchs, and palace women, pointing directly at the present without reserve.

sentences.zh: 杜衍、韓琦薦，擢太子中允、直集賢院。

translations.literal: Du Yan and Han Qi recommended him; he was promoted to Principal Collator of the Crown Prince and Academician of the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan and Han Qi recommended him, and he was promoted to Principal Collator of the Crown Prince and Academician of the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 會呂夷簡罷相，夏竦既除樞密使，復奪之，以衍代。

translations.literal: When Lü Yijian was dismissed as chancellor, Xia Song was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs but it was revoked again, with Yan replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Yijian was dismissed as chancellor, Xia Song was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs but the appointment was revoked again, with Yan replacing him.

sentences.zh: 章得象、晏殊、賈昌朝、范仲淹、富弼及琦同時執政，歐陽修、余靖、王素、蔡襄並為諫官，介喜曰：「此盛事也，歌頌吾職，其可已乎」作《慶曆聖德詩》，曰：

translations.literal: Zhang Dexiang, Yan Shu, Jia Changchao, Fan Zhongyan, Fu Bi, and Qi all held power simultaneously; Ouyang Xiu, Yu Jing, Wang Su, and Cai Xiang were all remonstrance officials. Jie rejoiced and said, "This is a grand occasion; singing praise is my duty—how could it stop?" He composed Ode on the Sage Virtues of Qingli, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dexiang, Yan Shu, Jia Changchao, Fan Zhongyan, Fu Bi, and Han Qi all held power simultaneously; Ouyang Xiu, Yu Jing, Wang Su, and Cai Xiang all served as remonstrance officials. Jie rejoiced and said, "This is a grand occasion, and singing praise is my duty—how could I stop?" He composed the Ode on the Sage Virtues of Qingli, which begins:

sentences.zh: 於惟慶曆三年三月，皇帝龍興，徐出闈闥。

translations.literal: Ah, in the third month of the third year of Qingli, the Emperor arose like a dragon, slowly emerging from the inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ah—in the third month of the third year of Qingli, the Emperor arose like a dragon and slowly emerged from the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 晨坐太極，晝開閶闔。

translations.literal: In the morning he sat in the Supreme Ultimate Hall; at day he opened the Gate of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the morning he sat in the Supreme Ultimate Hall; at daybreak he opened the Gate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 躬覽英賢，手鉏奸枿。

translations.literal: He personally surveyed worthy men and personally uprooted treacherous weeds.
translations.idiomatic: He personally surveyed worthy men and personally uprooted treacherous weeds.

sentences.zh: 大聲渢渢，震搖六合。

translations.literal: Great sounds thundered, shaking the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: Great sounds thundered, shaking the six directions.

sentences.zh: 如乾之動，如雷之發。

translations.literal: Like the movement of Qian, like the release of thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Like the movement of Qian, like the bursting of thunder.

sentences.zh: 昆蟲躑躅，怪妖藏滅。

translations.literal: Insects trampled; strange omens and demons hid and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Insects trampled underfoot; strange omens and demons hid themselves and perished.

sentences.zh: 同明道初，天地嘉吉。

translations.literal: Same as the beginning of Mingdao—heaven and earth were auspicious and blessed.
translations.idiomatic: As at the beginning of the Mingdao era, heaven and earth were auspicious and blessed.

sentences.zh: 初聞皇帝，蹙然言曰：「予祖予父，付予大業，予恐失墜，實賴輔弼。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor heard and, frowning, said, "My ancestors and my father entrusted to me the great enterprise; I fear losing it—it truly depends on assistants.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Emperor heard and, frowning, said, "My ancestors and my father entrusted to me the great enterprise; I fear losing it—it truly depends on my assistants.

sentences.zh: 汝得象、殊，重慎微密。

translations.literal: You have Dexiang and Shu—greatly cautious and subtle.
translations.idiomatic: You have Dexiang and Shu—greatly cautious and subtle.

sentences.zh: 君相予久，予嘉君伐。

translations.literal: You have long assisted me; I praise your merit.
translations.idiomatic: You have long assisted me; I praise your merit.

sentences.zh: 君仍相予，笙鏞斯協。

translations.literal: You still assist me; bells and gongs are in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: You still assist me; bells and gongs are in harmony.

sentences.zh: 昌朝儒者，學問該洽。

translations.literal: Changchao is a Confucian scholar; his learning is comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao is a Confucian scholar; his learning is comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 與予論政，傅以經術。

translations.literal: He discusses government with me, instructing with classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He discusses government with me, instructing me with classical learning.

sentences.zh: 汝貳二相，庶績咸秩。

translations.literal: You two are vice chancellors; all achievements are orderly.
translations.idiomatic: You two serve as vice chancellors; all achievements are in good order.

sentences.zh: 惟汝仲淹，汝誠予察。

translations.literal: "Only you, Zhongyan—you truly are perceptive to me."
translations.idiomatic: "Only you, Zhongyan—you truly understand me."

sentences.zh: 太后乘勢，湯沸火熱。

translations.literal: "The Empress Dowager seized power; waters boiled and fire burned hot."
translations.idiomatic: "The Empress Dowager seized power; waters boiled and fire burned hot."

sentences.zh: 汝時小臣，危言嶪嶪。

translations.literal: "You were then a minor official; your bold words were perilous."
translations.idiomatic: "You were then a minor official; your bold words were perilous."

sentences.zh: 為予司諫，正予門闑。

translations.literal: "You remonstrated for me, correcting my gates."
translations.idiomatic: "You remonstrated for me and corrected my gates."

sentences.zh: 為予京兆，堲予讒說。

translations.literal: "You were Jingzhao Prefect for me, destroying slander against me."
translations.idiomatic: "You served as Jingzhao Prefect for me and destroyed slander against me."

sentences.zh: 賊叛予夏，往予式遏。

translations.literal: "Rebels betrayed me in Xia; you went to check them."
translations.idiomatic: "Rebels betrayed me in Xia; you went to check them."

sentences.zh: 六月酷日，大冬積雪。

translations.literal: "The scorching sun of the sixth month, heavy snow in deep winter."
translations.idiomatic: "The scorching sun of the sixth month, heavy snow in deep winter."

sentences.zh: 汝寒汝暑，同予士卒。

translations.literal: "You endured cold and heat along with my soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: "You endured cold and heat along with my soldiers."

sentences.zh: 予聞辛酸，汝不告乏。

translations.literal: "When I heard of your hardship, you did not complain of want."
translations.idiomatic: "When I heard of your hardship, you did not complain of want."

sentences.zh: 予晚得弼，予心弼悅。

translations.literal: "I late obtained Bi; my heart was delighted with Bi."
translations.idiomatic: "I came late to know Bi, and my heart was delighted with him."

sentences.zh: 弼每見予，無有私謁。

translations.literal: "Whenever Bi saw me, he never had private audiences."
translations.idiomatic: "Whenever Bi saw me, he never sought private audiences."

sentences.zh: 以道輔予，弼言深切。

translations.literal: "He assisted me with the Way; Bi's words were deep and earnest."
translations.idiomatic: "He assisted me with the Way; Bi's words were deep and earnest."

sentences.zh: 予不堯、舜，弼自笞罰。

translations.literal: "I am not Yao or Shun; Bi would himself scourge and punish."
translations.idiomatic: "I am not Yao or Shun; Bi would scourge and punish me himself."

sentences.zh: 諫官一年，疏奏滿篋。

translations.literal: "Remonstrance officials for one year; memorials filled baskets."
translations.idiomatic: "For one year the remonstrance officials served; memorials filled their baskets."

sentences.zh: 侍從周歲，忠力廑竭。

translations.literal: "Attendants for a full year; loyalty and strength were exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: "For a full year the attendants served; loyalty and strength were exhausted."

sentences.zh: 契丹忘義，檮杌饕餮。

translations.literal: "The Khitan forgot righteousness—Taowu and Taotie."
translations.idiomatic: "The Khitan forgot righteousness—they were like Taowu and Taotie."

sentences.zh: 敢侮大國，其辭慢悖。

translations.literal: "They dared insult the great state; their words were insolent and rebellious."
translations.idiomatic: "They dared insult the great state; their words were insolent and rebellious."

sentences.zh: 弼將予命，不畏不怯。

translations.literal: "Bi carried my command; neither fearful nor timid."
translations.idiomatic: "Bi carried my command; neither fearful nor timid."

sentences.zh: 卒復舊好，民得食褐。

translations.literal: "Finally restored old friendly relations; the people obtained coarse cloth."
translations.idiomatic: "At last old friendly relations were restored, and the people obtained coarse cloth to wear."

sentences.zh: 沙磧萬里，死生一節。

translations.literal: "Desert sands ten thousand li; life and death one integrity."
translations.idiomatic: "Across desert sands ten thousand li, he held one integrity in life and death."

sentences.zh: 視弼之膚，霜剝風裂。

translations.literal: "Looking at Bi's skin—frost stripped and wind cracked."
translations.idiomatic: "Looking at Bi's skin—frost had stripped it and wind had cracked it."

sentences.zh: 觀弼之心，煉金鍛鐵。

translations.literal: "Looking at Bi's heart—refined gold and forged iron."
translations.idiomatic: "Looking at Bi's heart—it was refined gold and forged iron."

sentences.zh: 寵名大官，以酬勞渴。

translations.literal: "Great official names as favor to repay his toil."
translations.idiomatic: "Great official titles were granted as favor to repay his toil."

sentences.zh: 弼辭不受，其志莫奪。

translations.literal: "Bi declined and did not accept; his will could not be taken."
translations.idiomatic: "Bi declined and did not accept; his will could not be swayed."

sentences.zh: 惟仲淹、弼，一夔一契。

translations.literal: "Only Zhongyan and Bi—one Kui, one Qi."
translations.idiomatic: "Only Zhongyan and Bi—one Kui, one Qi."

sentences.zh: 天實賚予，予其敢忽。

translations.literal: "Heaven truly bestows on me; how could I dare neglect it?"
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven truly bestows this on me; how could I dare neglect it?"

sentences.zh: 並來弼予，民無瘥劄。

translations.literal: "All come to assist me; the people have no affliction or wound."
translations.idiomatic: "All come to assist me, and the people suffer no affliction or wound."

sentences.zh: 曰衍汝來，汝予黃髮。

translations.literal: "He said, Yan, you come—you give me gray hair."
translations.idiomatic: "He said, 'Yan, you come—you give me gray hair.'"

sentences.zh: 事予二紀，毛禿齒豁。

translations.literal: "Serving me for two decades, hair bald and teeth gaping."
translations.idiomatic: "Serving me for two decades, with hair grown bald and teeth worn away."

sentences.zh: 心如一兮，率履弗越。

translations.literal: "Heart as one; in conduct never transgressing."
translations.idiomatic: "His heart was one; in conduct he never transgressed."

sentences.zh: 遂長樞府，兵政無蹶。

translations.literal: "Then long head of the Military Affairs Commission; military and government without stumble."
translations.idiomatic: "Then long head of the Military Affairs Commission; military and government affairs proceeded without stumble."

sentences.zh: 予早識琦，琦有奇骨。

translations.literal: "I early knew Qi; Qi had extraordinary bones."
translations.idiomatic: "I knew Qi early on; Qi possessed extraordinary character."

sentences.zh: 其器魁落，豈視扂楔。

translations.literal: "His capacity was grand and lofty—how could one regard him as a door bolt or wedge?"
translations.idiomatic: "His capacity was grand and lofty—how could one regard him as a mere door bolt or wedge?"

sentences.zh: 其人渾樸，不施剞劂。

translations.literal: "The man was simple and unadorned, without carving or cutting."
translations.idiomatic: "The man was simple and unadorned, without artifice or ornament."

sentences.zh: 可屬大事，敦厚如勃。

translations.literal: "He could be entrusted with great affairs, solid and generous like Bo."
translations.idiomatic: "He could be entrusted with great affairs, solid and generous like Chen Bo."

sentences.zh: 琦汝副衍，知人予哲。

translations.literal: "Qi, you assist Yan; in knowing men I am wise."
translations.idiomatic: "Qi, you assist Yan; in knowing men I am wise."

sentences.zh: 惟修惟靖，立朝䡾䡾。

translations.literal: "Only Xiu and Jing—standing at court, they speak forthrightly."
translations.idiomatic: "Only Xiu and Jing—standing at court, they speak forthrightly."

sentences.zh: 言論磥砢，忠誠特達。

translations.literal: "Their words are rugged and firm; loyalty and sincerity uniquely penetrating."
translations.idiomatic: "Their words are rugged and firm; their loyalty and sincerity uniquely penetrating."

sentences.zh: 祿微身賤，其志不怯。

translations.literal: "Salary meager and status low, yet their will is not timid."
translations.idiomatic: "Though their salaries were meager and their status low, their will was not timid."

sentences.zh: 嘗詆大官，亟遭貶黜。

translations.literal: "They once denounced high officials and repeatedly suffered demotion."
translations.idiomatic: "They once denounced high officials and repeatedly suffered demotion."

sentences.zh: 萬里歸來，剛氣不折。

translations.literal: "Returning from ten thousand li, their firm spirit was not broken."
translations.idiomatic: "Returning from ten thousand li, their firm spirit was not broken."

sentences.zh: 屢進直言，以補予闕。

translations.literal: "Repeatedly advancing straight words to supplement my deficiencies."
translations.idiomatic: "They repeatedly advanced straight words to supplement my deficiencies."

sentences.zh: 素相之後，含忠履潔。

translations.literal: "Su, descendant of a chancellor—harboring loyalty and treading purity."
translations.idiomatic: "Su, descendant of a chancellor—harboring loyalty and treading the path of purity."

sentences.zh: 昔為御史，幾叩予榻。

translations.literal: "Formerly as censor, he nearly knocked at my couch."
translations.idiomatic: "Formerly as censor, he nearly knocked at my couch."

sentences.zh: 襄雖小官，名聞予徹。

translations.literal: "Xiang, though a minor official, his name reached me completely."
translations.idiomatic: "Xiang, though a minor official, his name reached me fully."

sentences.zh: 亦嘗獻言，箴予之失。

translations.literal: "He also once offered words, admonishing my faults."
translations.idiomatic: "He also once offered words, admonishing my faults."

sentences.zh: 剛守粹愨，與修儔匹。

translations.literal: "Firm in integrity, pure and honest—a match for Xiu."
translations.idiomatic: "Firm in integrity, pure and honest—a match for Xiu."

sentences.zh: 並為諫官，正色在列。

translations.literal: "All serving as remonstrance officials, with stern countenance in the ranks."
translations.idiomatic: "All serving as remonstrance officials, with stern countenance in the ranks."

sentences.zh: 予過汝言，毋鉗汝舌。」

translations.literal: "If I fault your words, do not clamp your tongue."
translations.idiomatic: "If I fault your words, do not clamp your tongues."

sentences.zh: 皇帝聖明，忠邪辨別。

translations.literal: The Emperor is sage and bright, distinguishing loyalty from treachery.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor is sage and bright, distinguishing loyalty from treachery.

sentences.zh: 舉擢俊良，掃除妖魃。

translations.literal: He promotes the worthy and good and sweeps away evil demons.
translations.idiomatic: He promotes the worthy and good and sweeps away evil demons.

sentences.zh: 眾賢之進，如茅斯拔。

translations.literal: The advance of many worthies is like pulling up thatch.
translations.idiomatic: The advance of many worthies is like pulling up thatch.

sentences.zh: 大奸之去，如距斯脫。

translations.literal: The departure of great traitors is like a pestle slipping free.
translations.idiomatic: The departure of great traitors is like a pestle slipping free.

sentences.zh: 上倚輔弼，司予調燮。

translations.literal: Above he relies on assistants to manage my harmonizing.
translations.idiomatic: Above he relies on assistants to harmonize governance.

sentences.zh: 下賴諫諍，維予紀法。

translations.literal: Below he depends on remonstrance to maintain my laws and standards.
translations.idiomatic: Below he depends on remonstrance to maintain his laws and standards.

sentences.zh: 左右正人，無有邪孽。

translations.literal: Upright men at his side—no wicked evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: Upright men stand at his side, and no wicked evildoers remain.

sentences.zh: 予望太平，日不逾浹。

translations.literal: I look toward great peace, day by day not exceeding a full cycle.
translations.idiomatic: I look toward great peace, day by day drawing nearer.

sentences.zh: 皇帝嗣位，二十二年。

translations.literal: The Emperor succeeded to the throne for twenty-two years.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had succeeded to the throne for twenty-two years.

sentences.zh: 神武不殺，其默如淵。

translations.literal: Divinely martial yet not killing; in silence like an abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Divinely martial yet not killing; in silence he was like an abyss.

sentences.zh: 聖人不測，其動如天。

translations.literal: The sage cannot be fathomed; in movement like heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The sage cannot be fathomed; in movement he was like heaven.

sentences.zh: 賞罰在予，不失其權。

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments are in my hands; I do not lose their authority.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments were in his hands; he did not lose their authority.

sentences.zh: 恭己南面，退奸進賢。

translations.literal: Reverently holding himself, facing south, he removed the wicked and advanced the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently holding himself and facing south, he removed the wicked and advanced the worthy.

sentences.zh: 知賢不易，非明弗得。

translations.literal: Knowing the worthy is not easy; without clarity one cannot attain it.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the worthy is not easy; without clarity one cannot attain it.

sentences.zh: 去邪惟艱，惟斷乃克。

translations.literal: Removing evil is only difficult; only through decisiveness can it be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Removing evil is difficult; only through decisiveness can it be achieved.

sentences.zh: 明則不貳，斷則不惑。

translations.literal: With clarity there is no duplicity; with decisiveness there is no confusion.
translations.idiomatic: With clarity there is no duplicity; with decisiveness there is no confusion.

sentences.zh: 既明且斷，惟皇帝之德。

translations.literal: Both clear and decisive—this is the virtue of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Both clear and decisive—such is the virtue of the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 群臣踧踖，重屏息，交相教語：曰惟正直，毋作側僻，皇帝汝殛。

translations.literal: The ministers were apprehensive, holding their breath in awe, instructing one another: "Be only upright; do not act perversely—the Emperor will punish you."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were apprehensive, holding their breath in awe, instructing one another: "Be only upright; do not act perversely—the Emperor will punish you."

sentences.zh: 諸侯危栗，墜玉失舄，交相告語：皇帝神明，四時朝覲，謹修臣職。

translations.literal: The feudal lords were fearful and trembling, dropping jade and losing shoes, telling one another: "The Emperor is divine and bright; at the four seasons' audiences, diligently perform your duties as ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The feudal lords were fearful and trembling, dropping jade and losing shoes, telling one another: "The Emperor is divine and bright; at the four seasons' audiences, diligently perform your duties as ministers."

sentences.zh: 四夷走馬，墜鐙遺策，交相告語：皇帝英武，解兵修貢，永為屬國。

translations.literal: The four barbarians galloped their horses, dropping stirrups and leaving whips, telling one another: "The Emperor is heroic and martial; lay down arms and offer tribute, forever becoming vassal states."
translations.idiomatic: The four barbarians galloped their horses, dropping stirrups and leaving whips, telling one another: "The Emperor is heroic and martial; lay down arms and offer tribute, forever becoming vassal states."

sentences.zh: 皇帝一舉，群臣懾焉，諸侯畏焉，四夷服焉。

translations.literal: With one act of the Emperor, the ministers were awed, the feudal lords feared, and the four barbarians submitted.
translations.idiomatic: With one act of the Emperor, the ministers were awed, the feudal lords feared, and the four barbarians submitted.

sentences.zh: 臣願皇帝，壽萬千年。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes the Emperor ten thousand years of life.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes the Emperor ten thousand years of life.

sentences.zh: 詩所稱多一時名臣，其言大奸，蓋斥竦也。

translations.literal: The poem praised many famous ministers of the time; its words about a great traitor were probably directed at Song.
translations.idiomatic: The poem praised many famous ministers of the time; its words about a great traitor were probably directed at Xia Song.

sentences.zh: 詩且出，孫復曰：「子禍始於此矣。」

translations.literal: When the poem was about to be published, Sun Fu said, "Your disaster begins here."
translations.idiomatic: When the poem was about to be published, Sun Fu said, "Your disaster begins here."

sentences.zh: 介不畜馬，借馬而乘，出入大臣之門，頗招賓客，預政事，人多指目。

translations.literal: Jie did not keep horses; he borrowed horses to ride, going in and out of great ministers' gates, gathering many guests, participating in government affairs—many people pointed and stared.
translations.idiomatic: Jie did not keep horses; he borrowed horses to ride, going in and out of great ministers' gates, gathering many guests, and participating in government affairs—many people pointed and stared.

sentences.zh: 不自安，求出，通判濮州，未赴，卒。

translations.literal: Feeling ill at ease, he requested to leave, was appointed Vice Commissioner of Pu Prefecture, but before taking up the post he died.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling ill at ease, he requested to leave, was appointed Vice Commissioner of Pu Prefecture, but before taking up the post he died.

sentences.zh: 會徐狂人孔直溫謀反，搜其家，得介書。

translations.literal: When the madman Kong Zhiwen of Xu plotted rebellion, his home was searched and Jie's letters were found.
translations.idiomatic: When the madman Kong Zhiwen of Xu plotted rebellion, his home was searched and Jie's letters were found.

sentences.zh: 夏竦銜介甚，且欲中傷杜衍等，因言介詐死，北走契丹，請發棺以驗。

translations.literal: Xia Song bore great resentment toward Jie and also wished to harm Du Yan and others; he therefore said Jie had faked death and fled north to the Khitan, requesting that the coffin be opened for verification.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song bore great resentment toward Jie and also wished to harm Du Yan and others; he therefore claimed Jie had faked death and fled north to the Khitan, requesting that the coffin be opened for verification.

sentences.zh: 詔下京東訪其存亡。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to the Jingdong circuit to investigate whether he was alive or dead.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to the Jingdong circuit to investigate whether he was alive or dead.

sentences.zh: 衍時在兗州，以驗介事語官屬，眾不敢答，掌書記龔鼎臣願以闔族保介必死，衍探懷出奏稿示之，曰：「老夫已保介矣。

translations.literal: Yan was then in Yan Prefecture; speaking of verifying Jie's case to his staff, none dared reply. Chief Secretary Gong Dingchen wished to guarantee with his entire clan that Jie was certainly dead. Yan drew from his breast a memorial draft and showed it, saying, "This old man has already guaranteed Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was then in Yan Prefecture; when he spoke of verifying Jie's case to his staff, none dared reply. Chief Secretary Gong Dingchen offered to guarantee with his entire clan that Jie was certainly dead. Yan drew a memorial draft from his breast and showed it, saying, "This old man has already guaranteed Jie.

sentences.zh: 君年少，見義必為，豈可量哉。」

translations.literal: You are young; seeing righteousness you must act—how can one measure such a person?"
translations.idiomatic: You are young; seeing righteousness you must act—how can one measure such a person?"

sentences.zh: 提點刑獄呂居簡亦曰：「發棺空，介果走北，孥戮非酷。

translations.literal: Judicial Commissioner Lü Jujian also said, "If the coffin is opened and empty, and Jie truly fled north, punishing his family would not be excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial Commissioner Lü Jujian also said, "If the coffin is opened and empty, and Jie truly fled north, punishing his family would not be excessive.

sentences.zh: 不然，是國家無故剖人塚墓，何以示後世？

translations.literal: Otherwise, the state would for no reason excavate a person's tomb—how could this be shown to later generations?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, the state would for no reason excavate a person's tomb—how could this be shown to later generations?

sentences.zh: 且介死必有親族門生會葬及棺斂之人，苟召問無異，即令具軍令狀保之，亦足應詔。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when Jie died there must have been relatives, disciples at the funeral, and those who placed him in the coffin; if summoned and questioned without discrepancy, then have them submit military pledge forms guaranteeing it—that would suffice to respond to the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Jie died there must have been relatives, disciples at the funeral, and those who placed him in the coffin; if summoned and questioned without discrepancy, then have them submit military pledge forms guaranteeing it—that would suffice to respond to the edict."

sentences.zh: 於是眾數百保介已死，乃免斫棺。

translations.literal: Thereupon several hundred people guaranteed that Jie was already dead, and opening the coffin was waived.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon several hundred people guaranteed that Jie was already dead, and opening the coffin was waived.

sentences.zh: 子弟羈管他州，久之得還。

translations.literal: His sons and younger brothers were detained in other prefectures; after a long time they were allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and younger brothers were detained in other prefectures; after a long time they were allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 介家故貧，妻子幾凍餒，富弼、韓琦共分奉買田以贍養之。

translations.literal: Jie's family was originally poor; his wife and children nearly froze and starved; Fu Bi and Han Qi together divided their salaries to buy land to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's family was originally poor; his wife and children nearly froze and starved; Fu Bi and Han Qi together divided their salaries to buy land to support them.

sentences.zh: 有《徂徠集》行於世。

translations.literal: There is the Culai Collection circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Culai Collection circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 胡瑗，字翼之，泰州海陵人。

translations.literal: Hu Yuan, courtesy name Yizhi, was a man of Hailing in Tai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuan, courtesy name Yizhi, was a native of Hailing in Tai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以經術教授吳中，年四十餘。

translations.literal: He taught classical learning in Wu, at over forty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He taught classical learning in Wu, at over forty years of age.

sentences.zh: 景祐初，更定雅樂，詔求知音者。
