translations.literal: In the early Jingyou era, when court music was revised, an edict sought those who understood music.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jingyou era, when court music was revised, an edict sought those who understood music.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹薦瑗，白衣對崇政殿。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan recommended Yuan; in plain clothes he answered at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan recommended Yuan, who in plain clothes answered at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 與鎮東軍節度推官阮逸同較鍾律，分造鍾磬各一虡。

translations.literal: Together with Military Commissioner Staff Officer Ruan Yi of Zhendong Army, he compared pitch standards and separately cast one set each of bells and chime-stones.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Military Commissioner Staff Officer Ruan Yi of Zhendong Army, he compared pitch standards and separately cast one set each of bells and chime-stones.

sentences.zh: 以一黍之廣為分，以製尺，律徑三分四厘六毫四絲，圍十分三厘九毫三絲。

translations.literal: Using the width of one millet grain as a fen, he made a measuring rod; the pitch-pipe diameter was three fen, four li, six hao, and four si; the circumference was ten fen, three li, nine hao, and three si.
translations.idiomatic: Using the width of one millet grain as a fen, he made a measuring rod; the pitch-pipe diameter was three fen, four li, six hao, and four si; the circumference was ten fen, three li, nine hao, and three si.

sentences.zh: 又以大黍累尺，小黍實龠。

translations.literal: He also used large millet to accumulate the foot measure and small millet to fill the yue vessel.
translations.idiomatic: He also used large millet to accumulate the foot measure and small millet to fill the yue vessel.

sentences.zh: 丁度等以為非古制，罷之，授瑗試秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Ding Du and others considered this not the ancient system and discontinued it; Yuan was appointed Trial Proofreader of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Du and others considered this not the ancient system and discontinued it; Yuan was appointed Trial Proofreader of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹經略陝西，辟丹州推官。

translations.literal: When Fan Zhongyan administered Shaanxi, he recruited Yuan as Staff Officer of Dan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan administered Shaanxi, he recruited Yuan as Staff Officer of Dan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以保寧節度推官教授湖州。

translations.literal: As Military Commissioner Staff Officer of Baoning, he taught in Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As Military Commissioner Staff Officer of Baoning, he taught in Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瑗教人有法，科條纖悉備具，以身先之。

translations.literal: Yuan had methods for teaching people; regulations were minutely detailed and complete, and he personally led by example.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had methods for teaching; regulations were minutely detailed and complete, and he personally led by example.

sentences.zh: 雖盛暑，必公服坐堂上，嚴師弟子之禮。

translations.literal: Even in great heat he always wore official robes and sat in the hall, strictly observing the rites between teacher and disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Even in great heat he always wore official robes and sat in the hall, strictly observing the rites between teacher and disciples.

sentences.zh: 視諸生如其子弟，諸生亦信愛如其父兄，從之遊者常數百人。

translations.literal: He regarded his students as his own sons and younger brothers; the students also trusted and loved him as their father and elder brothers; those who followed him numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He regarded his students as his own sons and younger brothers; the students also trusted and loved him as their father and elder brothers; those who followed him numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，興太學，下湖州取其法，著為令。

translations.literal: During Qingli the Imperial Academy was revived; the method was taken from Hu Prefecture and established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingli the Imperial Academy was revived; the method was taken from Hu Prefecture and established as regulation.

sentences.zh: 召為諸王宮教授，辭疾不行。

translations.literal: He was summoned as instructor for the Princes' Palaces but declined on grounds of illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as instructor for the Princes' Palaces but declined on grounds of illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 為太子中舍，以殿中丞致仕。

translations.literal: He became Principal Collator of the Crown Prince and retired as Palace Director.
translations.idiomatic: He became Principal Collator of the Crown Prince and retired as Palace Director.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，更鑄太常鍾磬，驛召瑗、逸，與近臣、太常官議於秘閣，遂典作樂事。

translations.literal: During Huangyou the bells and chime-stones of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were recast; Yuan and Yi were summoned by courier to discuss with near ministers and Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials in the Secret Pavilion, and Yuan then directed music-making affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou the bells and chime-stones of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices were recast; Yuan and Yi were summoned by courier to discuss with near ministers and Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials in the Secret Pavilion, and Yuan then directed music-making affairs.

sentences.zh: 復以大理評事兼太常寺主簿，辭不就。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review concurrently as Registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review concurrently as Registrar of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，授光祿寺丞、國子監直講。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Instructor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Instructor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 樂成，遷大理寺丞，賜緋衣銀魚。

translations.literal: When the music was completed, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and granted a red robe and silver fish badge.
translations.idiomatic: When the music was completed, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and granted a red robe and silver fish badge.

sentences.zh: 瑗既居太學，其徒益眾，太學至不能容，取旁官舍處之。

translations.literal: Once Yuan was at the Imperial Academy, his disciples grew ever more numerous; the Academy could no longer contain them, and nearby official quarters were taken to house them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan was at the Imperial Academy, his disciples grew ever more numerous; the Academy could no longer contain them, and nearby official quarters were taken to house them.

sentences.zh: 禮部所得士，瑗弟子十常居四五，隨材高下，喜自修飭，衣服容止，往往相類，人遇之雖不識，皆知其瑗弟子也。

translations.literal: Of those who passed the Ministry of Rites examination, four or five out of ten were often Yuan's disciples; according to their talent, high or low, they delighted in self-cultivation; dress and bearing were often alike—though people did not know them when they met them, all knew they were Yuan's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who passed the Ministry of Rites examination, four or five out of ten were often Yuan's disciples; according to their talent, high or low, they delighted in self-cultivation; their dress and bearing were often alike—though people did not know them when they met them, all knew they were Yuan's disciples.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐初，擢太子中允、天章閣侍講，仍治太學。

translations.literal: In the early Jiayou era he was promoted to Principal Collator of the Crown Prince and Lecturer of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, still administering the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jiayou era he was promoted to Principal Collator of the Crown Prince and Lecturer of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, still administering the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 既而疾不能朝，以太常博士致仕，歸老於家。

translations.literal: Soon afterward illness prevented him from attending court; he retired as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and returned home in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward illness prevented him from attending court; he retired as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and returned home in old age.

sentences.zh: 諸生與朝士祖餞東門外，時以為榮。

translations.literal: Students and court officials saw him off with a farewell feast outside the east gate; at the time this was considered an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Students and court officials saw him off with a farewell feast outside the east gate; at the time this was considered an honor.

sentences.zh: 既卒，詔賻其家。

translations.literal: After he died, an edict granted funeral funds to his family.
translations.idiomatic: After he died, an edict granted funeral funds to his family.

sentences.zh: 劉羲叟，字仲更，澤州晉城人。

translations.literal: Liu Xisou, courtesy name Zhonggeng, was a man of Jincheng in Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xisou, courtesy name Zhonggeng, was a native of Jincheng in Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修使河東，薦其學術。

translations.literal: When Ouyang Xiu was envoy to Hedong, he recommended his learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang Xiu served as envoy to Hedong, he recommended his learning.

sentences.zh: 試大理評事，權趙州軍事判官。

translations.literal: He passed examination for Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review and served as Acting Military Judge of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed examination for Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review and served as Acting Military Judge of Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 精算術，兼通《大衍》諸曆。

translations.literal: He was skilled in calculation and also mastered the various calendars of the Dayan system.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in calculation and also mastered the various calendars of the Dayan system.

sentences.zh: 及修唐史，令專修《律曆》、《天文》、《五行志》。

translations.literal: When the History of Tang was compiled, he was ordered to specialize in compiling the Treatises on Pitch Pipes and Calendars, Astronomy, and the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: When the History of Tang was compiled, he was ordered to specialize in compiling the Treatises on Pitch Pipes and Calendars, Astronomy, and the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 尋為編修官，改秘書省著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Soon he became a compilation officer and was transferred to Assistant Compiler of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became a compilation officer and was transferred to Assistant Compiler of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 以母喪去，詔令家居編修。

translations.literal: He left on mourning for his mother; an edict ordered him to compile at home.
translations.idiomatic: He left on mourning for his mother; an edict ordered him to continue compiling at home.

sentences.zh: 書成，擢崇文院檢討，未入謝，疽發背卒。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was promoted to Examiner of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; before entering to give thanks, a carbuncle erupted on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was completed, he was promoted to Examiner of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; before entering to give thanks, a carbuncle erupted on his back and he died.

sentences.zh: 羲叟強記多識，尤長於星曆、術數。

translations.literal: Xisou had a strong memory and wide knowledge, especially excelling in astronomy, calendrics, and numerology.
translations.idiomatic: Xisou had a strong memory and wide knowledge, especially excelling in astronomy, calendrics, and numerology.

sentences.zh: 皇祐五年，日食心，時胡瑗鑄鍾弇而直，聲鬱不發。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangyou there was a central solar eclipse; at the time Hu Yuan's cast bells were narrow and straight, and their sound was muffled and did not ring out.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huangyou there was a central solar eclipse; at the time Hu Yuan's cast bells were narrow and straight, and their sound was muffled and did not ring out.

sentences.zh: 又陝西鑄大錢，羲叟曰：「此所謂害金再興，與周景王同占，上將感心腹之疾。」

translations.literal: Also, large coins were cast in Shaanxi; Xisou said, "This is what is called harmful metal rising again—same omen as King Jing of Zhou; the ruler will suffer illness of the heart and abdomen."
translations.idiomatic: Also, large coins were cast in Shaanxi; Xisou said, "This is what is called harmful metal rising again—the same omen as King Jing of Zhou; the ruler will suffer illness of the heart and abdomen."

sentences.zh: 其後仁宗果不豫。

translations.literal: Afterward Emperor Renzong indeed fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Emperor Renzong indeed fell ill.

sentences.zh: 又月入太微，曰：「後宮當有喪。」

translations.literal: Again, when the moon entered the Supreme Palace, he said, "The inner palace will have a bereavement."
translations.idiomatic: When the moon later entered the Supreme Palace constellation, he predicted, "There will be a death in the inner palace."

sentences.zh: 已而張貴妃薨。

translations.literal: Before long, Noble Consort Zhang passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, Noble Consort Zhang died.

sentences.zh: 至和元年，日食正陽，客星出於昴，曰：「契丹宗真其死乎？」

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe, a solar eclipse occurred at noon, and a guest star appeared in the Pleiades; he said, "Has the Khitan ruler Zongzhen died?"
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhihe era, there was a central solar eclipse at midday and a guest star appeared in the Pleiades. He asked, "Has the Khitan emperor Zongzhen died?"

sentences.zh: 事皆驗。

translations.literal: All these matters were verified.
translations.idiomatic: In every case, his predictions came true.

sentences.zh: 羲叟未病，嘗曰：「吾及秋必死。」

translations.literal: Before Xisou fell ill, he once said, "I will certainly die by autumn."
translations.idiomatic: Even before he took sick, Xisou had said, "I am sure to die before autumn is out."

sentences.zh: 自擇地於父塚旁，占庚穴，以語其妻，如其言葬之。

translations.literal: He himself chose a site beside his father's tomb, divined a geng-day burial spot, told his wife, and was buried as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: He chose a grave site next to his father's tomb, selected an auspicious geng-day burial place, told his wife of his plans, and was interred exactly as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 著《十三代史志》、《劉氏輯曆》、《春秋災異》諸書。

translations.literal: He authored such books as Monographs on Thirteen Dynasties, Liu's Collected Calendars, and Portents and Anomalies in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Monographs on Thirteen Dynasties, Liu's Collected Calendars, Portents and Anomalies in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and other works.

sentences.zh: 林概，字端父，福州福清人。

translations.literal: Lin Gai, courtesy name Duanfu, was a man of Fuqing in Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Gai, courtesy name Duanfu, was a native of Fuqing in Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父高，太常博士，有治行。

translations.literal: His father Gao was a Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and had a record of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao served as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was known for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 概幼警悟，舉進士，以秘書省校書郎知長興縣。

translations.literal: Gai was quick-witted from youth; he passed the jinshi examination and, as Proofreader of the Secretariat, served as magistrate of Changxing County.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was precocious as a boy. After passing the jinshi examination, he was appointed Proofreader of the Secretariat and assigned as magistrate of Changxing County.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，富人閉糴以邀價，概出奉粟庭下，誘士豪輸數千石以飼饑者。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine, the rich hoarded grain to force up prices; Gai brought out his salary grain to the courtyard and induced local magnates to contribute several thousand shi to feed the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe famine, wealthy families hoarded grain to drive up prices. Gai put his official salary grain in the courtyard and persuaded local elites to donate thousands of shi to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 知連州。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Lian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Lian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 康定初，上封事曰：「古者民為兵，而今兵食民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangding era, he submitted a sealed memorial saying, "In antiquity the people were the army; today the army feeds on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangding era, he submitted a sealed memorial stating, "In ancient times the people themselves were the army; now the army lives off the people.

sentences.zh: 古馬寓於民，而今不習馬。

translations.literal: In antiquity horses were kept among the people; today they do not train with horses.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity horses were distributed among the populace; today men no longer train in horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 此兵與馬之大患也。

translations.literal: These are the great afflictions of soldiers and horses.
translations.idiomatic: These are the gravest problems facing our armies and our cavalry.

sentences.zh: 請附唐府兵之法，四斂一民，部以為軍，閑耕田里，被甲皆兵。

translations.literal: He requested adoption of the Tang militia system: from every four households one man is levied, organized into units as an army, farming in idle seasons in the fields, and when armored all become soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed reviving the Tang frontier-militia system: draft one man from every four households, organize them into military units, let them farm in peacetime, and treat every armed man as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 因命其家咸得畜馬，私乘休暇，官為調習。

translations.literal: Accordingly he ordered that every household be allowed to keep horses, riding privately on rest days while officials provided drill and training.
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered every household to keep horses, allowing private riding on days off while the government organized regular training.

sentences.zh: 則人便干戈，馬識行列。

translations.literal: Then men would be practiced with weapons, and horses would know ranks and files.
translations.idiomatic: Thus men would grow accustomed to arms, and horses would learn to move in formation.

sentences.zh: 又行陣無法，而出於臨時；

translations.literal: Moreover, battle formations have no fixed methods and are improvised on the spot;
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that armies had no standard battle formations and improvised them at the last moment;

sentences.zh: 將無素備，而取於倉卒；

translations.literal: generals have no standing preparation and are chosen in haste;
translations.idiomatic: generals received no advance training and were appointed in emergencies;

sentences.zh: 軍不予權，而監以宦侍：若是者，雖得古之材，使循今之法，亦必屢戰而屢敗。」

translations.literal: armies are not granted authority but are supervised by eunuch attendants: in such conditions, even with talent of antiquity, if made to follow present methods, they would surely fight repeatedly and lose repeatedly."
translations.idiomatic: and armies were denied real command while eunuch overseers watched over them. Under such conditions, even ancient-worthy talent forced to obey today's methods would fight battle after battle and lose again and again."

sentences.zh: 又請備蠻，籍土民為兵，柵要衝，購徭人使守禦。

translations.literal: He also requested preparations against the barbarians: register native inhabitants as soldiers, fortify strategic passes, and hire corvée laborers for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged defenses against the southern tribes: enroll local people as militia, build stockades at key passes, and hire corvée workers to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 徙淮安軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huai'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Huai'an Army.

sentences.zh: 程琳嘗禁蜀人不得自為渠堰，概奏罷之。

translations.literal: Cheng Lin had once forbidden the people of Shu from building their own canals and dikes; Gai memorialized and had the ban repealed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lin had prohibited Sichuan residents from constructing their own irrigation works; Gai submitted a memorial that got the prohibition lifted.

sentences.zh: 又言蜀饑，願罷川峽漕，發常平粟貸民租，募富人輕粟價，除商旅之禁，使通貨相資。

translations.literal: He also said that Shu was suffering famine and requested abolishing the Sichuan transport commissioner, releasing Ever-Normal Granary grain to lend for people's rents, recruiting the wealthy to lower grain prices, removing travel and merchant prohibitions, and enabling circulating goods to assist one another.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported famine in Sichuan and proposed abolishing the Sichuan transport office, distributing Ever-Normal Granary grain on loan to cover peasants' rents, encouraging wealthy merchants to lower grain prices, lifting travel restrictions on traders, and allowing goods to circulate freely.

sentences.zh: 官至太常博士、集賢校理，卒。

translations.literal: He reached the offices of Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies before his death.

sentences.zh: 著《史論》、《辨國語》。

translations.literal: He authored Discourses on History and Critique of the Discourses of the States.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Discourses on History and Critique of the Discourses of the States.

sentences.zh: 子希，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Xi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi is given a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 李覯，字泰伯，建昌軍南城人。

translations.literal: Li Gou, courtesy name Taibo, was a man of Nancheng in Jianchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gou, courtesy name Taibo, was a native of Nancheng in Jianchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 俊辯能文，舉茂才異等不中。

translations.literal: Talented in debate and skilled in writing, he entered the Outstanding Talent special examination but was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and an able writer, he took the Outstanding Talent special examination but failed to pass.

sentences.zh: 親老，以教授自資，學者常數十百人。

translations.literal: His parents were aged; he supported himself by teaching, and students regularly numbered in the dozens or hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: With elderly parents to support, he made his living as a teacher, and his students often numbered in the dozens or even hundreds.

sentences.zh: 皇祐初，范仲淹薦為試太學助教，上《明堂定制圖序》曰：

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangyou, Fan Zhongyan recommended him as probationary Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy; he submitted A Preface to the Diagram of the Bright Hall's Prescribed Design, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huangyou era, Fan Zhongyan recommended him for probationary Assistant Instructor at the Imperial Academy. Gou submitted A Preface to the Diagram of the Bright Hall's Prescribed Design, which reads:

sentences.zh: 《考工記》「周人明堂，度九尺之筵」，是言堂基修廣，非謂立室之數。

translations.literal: The Records of Examination of Crafts says, "The Zhou people's Bright Hall measures nine-chi mats"—this speaks of the length and breadth of the hall foundation, not the number of rooms to be erected.
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Examination of Crafts states, "The Zhou people's Bright Hall is measured in nine-chi mats." This refers to the dimensions of the hall platform, not to how many rooms should be built.

sentences.zh: 「東西九筵，南北七筵，堂崇一筵」，是言堂上，非謂室中。

translations.literal: "Nine mats east-west, seven mats north-south, hall height one mat"—this speaks of the upper hall, not the interior chambers.
translations.idiomatic: "Nine mats east to west, seven mats north to south, and one mat in height" describes the hall above, not the rooms within.

sentences.zh: 東西之堂各深四筵半，南北之堂各深三筵半。

translations.literal: The east and west halls are each four and a half mats deep; the north and south halls are each three and a half mats deep.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern and western halls each extend four and a half mats in depth; the northern and southern halls each extend three and a half mats.

sentences.zh: 「五室，凡室二筵」，是言四堂中央有方十筵之地，自東至西可營五室，自南至北可營五室。

translations.literal: "Five chambers, each chamber two mats in all"—this means that in the center of the four halls there is a square space of ten mats; from east to west five chambers can be built, and from south to north five chambers can be built.
translations.idiomatic: "Five chambers, each two mats across" means that at the center of the four halls lies a square area ten mats on a side, wide enough to accommodate five chambers from east to west and five from south to north.

sentences.zh: 十筵中央方二筵之地，既為太室，連作餘室，則不能令十二位各直其辰，當於東南西北四面及四角缺處，各虛方二筵之地，周而通之，以為太廟。

translations.literal: The central two-mat square within the ten mats, being made the Grand Chamber and connected with the remaining chambers, cannot allow the twelve positions each to align with its season; at the gaps on the southeast, northwest, four sides, and four corners, each should leave empty a two-mat square, opened all around and connected, to serve as the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: If the central two-mat square within the ten-mat area is made the Grand Chamber and joined directly to the other rooms, the twelve seasonal positions cannot each face its proper direction. At the open spaces on the four sides and four corners, one should therefore leave two-mat squares, linked all around into a circuit, to form the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 太室正居中，《月令》所謂「中央土」、「居太廟太室」者，言此太廟之中有太室也。

translations.literal: The Grand Chamber stands directly at the center; what the Ordinances of the Months call "central earth" and "dwelling in the Grand Temple, Grand Chamber" means that within this Grand Temple there is a Grand Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Chamber sits at the exact center. When the Ordinances of the Months speak of "central earth" and "dwelling in the Grand Temple's Grand Chamber," they mean that the Grand Temple encloses a Grand Chamber at its heart.

sentences.zh: 太廟之外，當子、午、卯、酉四位上各畫方二筵地，以與太廟相通，為青陽、明堂、總章、元堂四太廟；

translations.literal: Outside the Grand Temple, at the four positions of zi, wu, mao, and you, mark out a two-mat square on each, connected to the Grand Temple, forming the four Grand Temples of Qingyang, Mingtang, Zongzhang, and Yuantang;
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Grand Temple, at the four cardinal points of zi, wu, mao, and you, one should mark out a two-mat square on each side, linked to the Grand Temple, to form the four seasonal halls of Qingyang, Mingtang, Zongzhang, and Yuantang;

sentences.zh: 當寅、申、巳、亥、辰、戌、醜、未八位上各畫方二筵地，以為左個、右個也。

translations.literal: at the eight positions of yin, shen, si, hai, chen, xu, chou, and wei, mark out a two-mat square on each to serve as the left and right annex chambers.
translations.idiomatic: and at the eight intermediate directions of yin, shen, si, hai, chen, xu, chou, and wei, mark out a two-mat square on each to serve as the left and right annex chambers.

sentences.zh: 《大戴禮·盛德記》：「明堂凡九室，室四戶八牖，共三十六戶、七十二牖。」

translations.literal: The Elder Dai's Book of Rites, Record of Full Virtue: "The Bright Hall has nine chambers in all; each chamber has four doors and eight windows, totaling thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows."
translations.idiomatic: The Elder Dai's Book of Rites, Record of Full Virtue, states: "The Bright Hall comprises nine chambers in all. Each chamber has four doors and eight windows, for a total of thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows."

sentences.zh: 八個之室，並太室而九，室四面各有戶，戶旁夾兩牖也。

translations.literal: The eight annex chambers together with the Grand Chamber make nine; each chamber has a door on each of its four sides, with two windows flanking each door.
translations.idiomatic: The eight annex chambers plus the Grand Chamber make nine rooms in all. Each chamber has a door on every side, with two windows set beside each door.

sentences.zh: 《白虎通》：「明堂上圓下方，八窗、四闥、九室、十二坐。」

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Discussion in the White Tiger Hall: "The Bright Hall is round above and square below, with eight windows, four doorways, nine chambers, and twelve seats."
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Discussion in the White Tiger Hall says: "The Bright Hall is round on top and square below, with eight windows, four doorways, nine chambers, and twelve thrones."

sentences.zh: 四太廟前各為一門，出於堂上，門旁夾兩窗也。

translations.literal: Before each of the four Grand Temples there is one gate opening onto the hall, with two windows flanking each gate.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the four seasonal halls has a gate in front opening onto the main hall, with two windows set beside every gate.

sentences.zh: 左右之個其實皆室，但以分處左右，形如夾房，故有個名。

translations.literal: The left and right annexes are in fact all chambers, but because they are placed separately to left and right in the form of wing rooms, they are called annexes.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right annex chambers are really full rooms, but because they stand to either side like flanking wings, they are given the special name ge, "annex."

sentences.zh: 太廟之內以及太室，其實祀文王配上帝之位，謂之廟者，義當然矣。

translations.literal: Within the Grand Temple and the Grand Chamber, what is actually enshrined is the place where King Wen is paired with the Lord on High; that it is called a temple is naturally fitting in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Grand Temple and the Grand Chamber, the rites actually enshrine King Wen alongside the Lord on High. Calling the structure a temple is therefore entirely appropriate.

sentences.zh: 土者分王四時，於五行最尊，故天子當其時居太室，用祭天地之位以尊嚴之也。

translations.literal: Earth divides kingship over the four seasons and is most honored among the Five Phases; therefore when the season arrives the Son of Heaven dwells in the Grand Chamber, using the position of sacrificing to Heaven and Earth to give it solemn dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Earth reigns over the four seasons and holds the highest place among the Five Phases. Accordingly, when that season arrives the Son of Heaven resides in the Grand Chamber, occupying the place reserved for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth to honor it with due majesty.

sentences.zh: 四仲之月，各得一時之中，與餘月有異。

translations.literal: The four mid-season months each obtain the middle of a season and differ from the remaining months.
translations.idiomatic: The four mid-season months each mark the midpoint of a season and therefore differ from the other months.

sentences.zh: 故復於子、午、卯、酉之方，取二筵地，假太廟之名以聽朔也。

translations.literal: Therefore again at the directions of zi, wu, mao, and you, two-mat plots are taken and, borrowing the name Grand Temple, used for listening to the new moon proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason, at the four directions of zi, wu, mao, and you, two-mat plots are set aside and, under the borrowed name of Grand Temple, used for the ceremony of announcing the new moon.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》言基而不及室，《大戴》言室而不及廟，稽之《月令》則備矣，然非《白虎通》，亦無以知窗闥之制也。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou speaks of the foundation but not the chambers; the Elder Dai speaks of chambers but not the temple; checked against the Ordinances of the Months it is complete—yet without the Comprehensive Discussion in the White Tiger Hall, there is no way to know the system of windows and doorways.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou describes the foundation but not the rooms; the Elder Dai describes the rooms but not the temple precinct. Cross-checked with the Ordinances of the Months, the account becomes complete—yet only the Comprehensive Discussion in the White Tiger Hall reveals the design of windows and doorways.

sentences.zh: 聶崇義所謂秦人《明堂圖》者，其制有十二階，古之遺法，當亦取之。

translations.literal: What Nie Chongyi calls the Qin people's Diagram of the Bright Hall has in its design twelve steps—an ancient surviving method that should also be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The Diagram of the Bright Hall attributed by Nie Chongyi to the Qin includes twelve steps in its design. As a surviving ancient practice, that feature should be adopted as well.

sentences.zh: 《禮記外傳》曰：「明堂四面各五門。」

translations.literal: The Outer Commentary on the Book of Rites says: "The Bright Hall has five gates on each of its four sides."
translations.idiomatic: The Outer Commentary on the Book of Rites states: "The Bright Hall has five gates on each of its four sides."

sentences.zh: 今按《明堂位》：四夷之國，四門之外。

translations.literal: Now examining the Hall Positions: the states of the four barbarians are outside the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the Hall Positions, one finds that the states of the four barbarian quarters stand outside the four gates.

sentences.zh: 九采之國，應門之外。

translations.literal: The states of the nine colors are outside the Ying Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The states of the nine colors stand outside the Ying Gate.

sentences.zh: 時天子負斧扆南向而立。

translations.literal: At the time the Son of Heaven stood facing south with his back to the axe-and-screen.
translations.idiomatic: On these occasions the Son of Heaven stood facing south with his back to the axe-and-screen.

sentences.zh: 南門之外者北面東上，應門之外者亦北面東上，是南門之外有應門也。

translations.literal: Those outside the Southern Gate face north with east at the top; those outside the Ying Gate also face north with east at the top—thus outside the Southern Gate there is a Ying Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Those stationed outside the Southern Gate face north with east at the top, and those outside the Ying Gate do the same. This shows that the Ying Gate lies beyond the Southern Gate.

sentences.zh: 既有應門，則不得不有皋、庫、雉門。

translations.literal: Since there is a Ying Gate, there must also be the Gao, Ku, and Zhi gates.
translations.idiomatic: If there is a Ying Gate, the Gao, Ku, and Zhi gates must necessarily exist as well.

sentences.zh: 明堂者，四時所居，四面如一，南面既有五門，則餘三面皆各有五門。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is where the four seasons are dwelt in; its four sides are alike—if the south face already has five gates, then the remaining three sides each likewise have five gates.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall is the dwelling for all four seasons, and all four sides are identical in form. If the south face has five gates, the other three faces must each have five gates as well.

sentences.zh: 鄭注《明堂位》則雲「正門謂之應門」，其意當謂變南門之文以為應門。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary on Hall Positions says, "The main gate is called the Ying Gate"—his meaning is presumably to change the wording of Southern Gate into Ying Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary on Hall Positions says, "The main gate is called the Ying Gate." He apparently means simply to substitute the term Ying Gate for Southern Gate.

sentences.zh: 又見王宮有路門，其次乃有應門。

translations.literal: One also sees that the royal palace has a Road Gate, and next after it comes the Ying Gate.
translations.idiomatic: We also know that the royal palace has a Road Gate, with the Ying Gate standing next beyond it.

sentences.zh: 今明堂無路門之名，而但有應門，便謂更無重門，而南門即是應門。

translations.literal: Now the Bright Hall has no name of Road Gate but only Ying Gate, so some conclude there are no further inner gates and that the Southern Gate is itself the Ying Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Bright Hall records no Road Gate and mentions only the Ying Gate, some conclude that there are no additional inner gates and that the Southern Gate is the Ying Gate itself.

sentences.zh: 且路寢之前則名路門，其次有應門。

translations.literal: Moreover, before the Road Quarters is what is called the Road Gate, and next comes the Ying Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Road Quarters stands the Road Gate, and beyond it the Ying Gate.

sentences.zh: 明堂非路寢，乃變其內門之名為東門南門，而次有應門，何害於義？

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is not the Road Quarters; one may simply change the names of its inner gates to East Gate and South Gate, with the Ying Gate next—what harm is there to the meaning?
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall is not the Road Quarters, so why not rename its inner gates as the East Gate and South Gate, with the Ying Gate standing beyond? Where is the offense against ritual propriety in that?

sentences.zh: 四夷之君，既在四門之外，而外無重門，則是列於郊野道路之間，豈朝會之儀乎？

translations.literal: The lords of the four barbarians, being outside the four gates with no further inner gates beyond, would be lined up between suburban fields and roads—is that the protocol of court assembly?
translations.idiomatic: If the lords of the four quarters stand outside the four gates with no inner gates beyond, they would be arrayed out in the open countryside between roads. Could that possibly be the etiquette of a court audience?

sentences.zh: 王宮常居，猶設五門，以限中外。

translations.literal: The royal palace of regular residence still establishes five gates to demarcate inner from outer.
translations.idiomatic: Even the palace of everyday residence maintains five gates to separate the inner and outer domains.

sentences.zh: 明堂者，效天法地，尊祖配帝，而止一門以表之，豈為稱哉！

translations.literal: The Bright Hall emulates Heaven and takes Earth as its model, honors the ancestors and pairs them with the Lord on High—yet to represent it with only one gate, how could that be fitting!
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall emulates Heaven, conforms to Earth, honors the ancestors, and pairs them with the Lord on High—yet to symbolize all that with a single gate would be wholly inadequate!

sentences.zh: 若其建置之所，則淳於登雲「在國之陽，三里之外，七里之內，丙巳之地」。

translations.literal: As for the place of its construction, Chunyu Dengyun says, "In the yang of the state, outside three li and within seven li, in the bing-si direction."
translations.idiomatic: As for where it should be built, Chunyu Dengyun specifies "in the sunny south of the capital, between three and seven li from the city, in the southeast direction."

sentences.zh: 《玉藻》「聽朔於南門之外」，康成之注亦與是合。

translations.literal: The Jade Regalia says, "Listen to the new moon outside the Southern Gate," and Kang Cheng's commentary also agrees with this.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Regalia prescribes "announcing the new moon outside the Southern Gate," and Zheng Xuan's commentary agrees with this placement.

sentences.zh: 夫稱明也，宜在國之陽。

translations.literal: Being called "bright," it should be in the yang of the state.
translations.idiomatic: As its name "Bright Hall" implies, it ought to stand in the sunny south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 事天神也，宜在城門之外。

translations.literal: Serving the gods of Heaven, it should be outside the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: Because it serves the heavenly deities, it should lie outside the city gates.

sentences.zh: 今圖以九分當九尺之筵，東西之堂共九筵，南北之堂共七筵。

translations.literal: The present diagram uses nine parts to represent the nine-chi mat; the east-west halls total nine mats, and the north-south halls total seven mats.
translations.idiomatic: In the present diagram, nine parts stand for the nine-chi mat unit. The eastern and western halls together span nine mats, and the northern and southern halls together span seven mats.

sentences.zh: 中央之地自東至西凡五室，自南至北凡五室，每室二筵，取於《考工記》也。

translations.literal: The central area from east to west has five chambers in all, and from south to north five chambers in all, each chamber two mats—taken from the Records of Examination of Crafts.
translations.idiomatic: The central area accommodates five chambers from east to west and five from south to north, each two mats across—following the Records of Examination of Crafts.

sentences.zh: 一太室、八左右個，共九室，室有四戶、八牖，共三十六戶、七十二牖，協於戴德《記》也。

translations.literal: One Grand Chamber and eight left and right annexes, nine chambers in all; each chamber has four doors and eight windows, totaling thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows—accordant with Elder Dai's Record.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Chamber plus eight left and right annexes make nine chambers in all, each with four doors and eight windows—for thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows in total—in agreement with Elder Dai's Record.

sentences.zh: 九室四廟，共十三位，本於《月令》也。

translations.literal: Nine chambers and four temples, thirteen positions in all, rooted in the Ordinances of the Months.
translations.idiomatic: Nine chambers and four temples, thirteen positions in all, derive from the Ordinances of the Months.

sentences.zh: 四廟之面，各為一門，門夾兩窗，是為八窗四闥，稽於《白虎通》也。

translations.literal: The face of each of the four temples has one gate, with two windows flanking each gate—this makes eight windows and four doorways, checked against the Comprehensive Discussion in the White Tiger Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the four seasonal halls has one gate on its face, with two windows beside every gate—yielding eight windows and four doorways, as confirmed by the Comprehensive Discussion in the White Tiger Hall.

sentences.zh: 十二階，采於《三禮圖》也。

translations.literal: Twelve steps are taken from the Diagram of the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve steps are drawn from the Diagram of the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 四面各五門，酌於《明堂位》、《禮記外傳》也。

translations.literal: Five gates on each of the four sides are drawn from Hall Positions and the Outer Commentary on the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Five gates on each of the four sides follow Hall Positions and the Outer Commentary on the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，用國子監奏，召為海門主簿、太學說書而卒。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, upon the memorial of the Directorate of Education, he was summoned as Registrar of Haimen and Lecturer of the Imperial Academy, then died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou era, on the recommendation of the Directorate of Education, he was summoned to serve as Registrar of Haimen and Lecturer at the Imperial Academy, but died soon after taking office.

sentences.zh: 覯嘗著《周禮致太平論》、《平土書》、《禮論》。

translations.literal: Gou once authored On the Rites of Zhou for Bringing Great Peace, Book on Leveling the Land, and Discourses on Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Gou had written On the Rites of Zhou for Bringing Great Peace, Book on Leveling the Land, and Discourses on Ritual.

sentences.zh: 門人鄧潤甫，熙寧中，上其《退居類稿》、《皇祐續稿》並《後集》，請官其子參魯，詔以為郊社齋郎。

translations.literal: His disciple Deng Runpu, in the Xining era, submitted Gou's Classified Drafts from Retirement, Continued Drafts from Huangyou, and Later Collection, and requested an office for his son Canlu; an edict appointed him Suburban and Altar Acolyte.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era, his disciple Deng Runpu submitted Gou's Classified Drafts from Retirement, Continued Drafts from Huangyou, and Later Collection, and petitioned for an official post for Gou's son Canlu. An edict appointed Canlu Suburban and Altar Acolyte.

sentences.zh: 何涉，字濟川，南充人。

translations.literal: He She, courtesy name Jichuan, was a man of Nanchong.
translations.idiomatic: He She, courtesy name Jichuan, was a native of Nanchong.

sentences.zh: 父，祖皆業農，涉始讀書，晝夜刻苦，泛覽博古。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather both made farming their occupation; She first took up books, studying day and night with arduous effort, broadly reading and mastering antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: His father and grandfather had both been farmers. She began studying only later, working day and night with tireless dedication and reading widely across the classics of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 上自《六經》、諸子百家，旁及山經、地誌、醫卜之術，無所不學，一過目不復再讀，而終身不忘。

translations.literal: From the Six Classics and the hundred schools of philosophers on down to mountain classic, geographical gazetteer, and medical and divinatory arts—there was nothing he did not study; once he passed his eyes over it he did not read again, yet he never forgot it for life.
translations.idiomatic: From the Six Classics and the hundred schools down to mountain guides, geographical gazetteers, and medical and divinatory texts, he studied everything. He needed only a single reading and never looked at a text again, yet remembered it for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 人問書傳中事，必指卷第冊葉所在，驗之果然。

translations.literal: When people asked about matters in books and records, he always pointed out the scroll, fascicle, and leaf where they stood, and on checking it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: When asked about any passage in the classics, he could cite the exact scroll, fascicle, and page. Verification always proved him right.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，調洛交主簿，改中部令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as Registrar of Luojiao, and was changed to Magistrate of Zhongbu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Registrar of Luojiao, and later transferred to serve as magistrate of Zhongbu.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹一見奇之，辟彰武軍節度推官。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan, upon one meeting, considered him extraordinary and recruited him as Military Push Officer of the Zhangwu Army command.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan was struck by him at their first meeting and recruited him as Military Push Officer under the Zhangwu Army command.

sentences.zh: 用龐籍奏，遷著作佐郎、管勾鄜延等路經略安撫招討司機宜文字。

translations.literal: On Pang Ji's memorial he was promoted to Assistant Compiler and Staff Planner for Documents of the Yan-Yan and other Circuits Pacification, Appeasement, and Recruitment Commission.
translations.idiomatic: On Pang Ji's recommendation he was promoted to Assistant Compiler and appointed staff planner for the Yan-Yan and related circuits' Pacification, Appeasement, and Recruitment Commission.

sentences.zh: 時元昊擾邊，軍中經畫，涉預有力。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Hao was harassing the frontier; in the army's planning, She contributed strong effort.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuan Hao was raiding the frontier, and She played an important part in the army's strategic planning.

sentences.zh: 元昊納款，籍召為樞密使，欲與之俱，涉曰：「親老矣，非人子自便之時。」

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao submitted allegiance, Ji was summoned as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and wished to take him along; She said, "My parents are old—this is not a time for a son to seek his own convenience."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao submitted to the court, Pang Ji was recalled to serve as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and wanted She to accompany him. She replied, "My parents are elderly. This is no time for a son to put his own convenience first."

sentences.zh: 拜章願得歸養，特改秘書丞、通判眉州，徙嘉州。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting to return and support his parents; he was specially changed to Secretary of the Secretariat and Administrative Assistant of Mei Prefecture, then transferred to Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial asking to return home and care for his parents. He was specially appointed Secretary of the Secretariat and Administrative Assistant of Mei Prefecture, then transferred to Jia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 用文彥博、龐籍薦，召還，除集賢校理。

translations.literal: On the recommendations of Wen Yanbo and Pang Ji, he was recalled and appointed Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Wen Yanbo and Pang Ji, he was recalled to court and appointed Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 既又求歸蜀，遂得知漢州。

translations.literal: Then again he requested to return to Shu and was accordingly made prefect of Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to return to Sichuan and was appointed prefect of Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，移合州。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was transferred to He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he was transferred to He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累官尚書司封員外郎。

translations.literal: By accumulated offices he reached Assistant Director of the Ministry of Rites, Department of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites' Department of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 父喪，罷歸，卒。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he left office and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he resigned and returned home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 詔恤其家，並官其一子。

translations.literal: An edict granted relief to his household and also gave an office to one of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered relief for his family and granted an official post to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 涉長厚有操行，事親至孝，平居未嘗談人過惡。

translations.literal: She was generous and honest with moral conduct; in serving his parents he was utmost in filial piety; in ordinary life he never spoke of others' faults and wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: She was generous, honest, and principled. He was deeply filial toward his parents and never spoke ill of others in daily life.

sentences.zh: 所至多建學館，勸誨諸生，從之遊者甚眾。

translations.literal: Wherever he arrived he largely built academies, admonishing and instructing the students; those who followed him in study were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he served he founded schools, guiding and encouraging students, and a great many scholars came to study under him.

sentences.zh: 雖在軍中，亦嘗為諸將講《左氏春秋》，狄青之徒皆橫經以聽。

translations.literal: Even while in the army, he also once lectured the generals on Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals; Di Qing and his fellows all sat with the classic spread before them to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Even in camp he lectured the generals on Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals, and Di Qing and others all sat before him with the text open to listen.

sentences.zh: 有《治道中術》、《春秋本旨》、《廬江集》七十卷。

translations.literal: He had Arts of Governing the Way, Original Purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Lujiang Collection in seventy juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Arts of Governing the Way, Original Purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Lujiang Collection in seventy juan.

sentences.zh: 王回，字深父，福州候官人。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, courtesy name Shenfu, was a man of Houguan in Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, courtesy name Shenfu, was a native of Houguan in Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父平言，試御史。

translations.literal: His father Pingyan held the office of Probationary Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pingyan served as Probationary Censor.

sentences.zh: 回敦行孝友，質直平恕，造次必稽古人所為，而不為小廉曲謹以求名譽。

translations.literal: Hui earnestly practiced filial piety and brotherly affection; he was straightforward, impartial, and forgiving. In every action he examined what the ancients did, yet he did not engage in petty scrupulousness and narrow propriety to seek reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was deeply devoted to filial piety and brotherly affection, upright, fair-minded, and forgiving. In everything he did he measured himself against the conduct of the ancients, yet he refused to cultivate petty fastidiousness or strained propriety in pursuit of fame.

sentences.zh: 嘗舉進士中第，為衛真簿，有所不合，稱病自免。

translations.literal: He once passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Registrar of Weizhen; finding the post unsuitable, he claimed illness and resigned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: He once passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Weizhen County, but when the position did not suit him he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 作《告友》曰：

translations.literal: He composed "Admonishing Friends," which says:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote an essay called "Admonishing Friends," which says:

sentences.zh: 古之言天下達道者，曰君臣也，父子也。

translations.literal: When the ancients spoke of the universal Way under Heaven, they named ruler and minister, and father and son.
translations.idiomatic: When the ancients spoke of the universal relationships under Heaven, they named those between ruler and minister and between father and son.

sentences.zh: 夫婦也，兄弟也，朋友也。

translations.literal: Husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and friends.
translations.idiomatic: They also named those between husband and wife, between brothers, and between friends.

sentences.zh: 五者各以其義行而人倫立，其義廢則人倫亦從而亡矣。

translations.literal: These five, each practiced according to its proper principle, establish human relationships; when their principles are abandoned, human relationships likewise perish with them.
translations.idiomatic: These five relationships, each upheld according to its proper duty, establish the order of human society; when those duties are abandoned, that order collapses as well.

sentences.zh: 然而父子兄弟之親，天性之自然者也；

translations.literal: Yet the intimacy of father and son and of elder and younger brothers is something natural to innate disposition;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bond between father and son and between brothers arises from natural instinct;

sentences.zh: 夫婦之合，以人情而然者也；

translations.literal: the union of husband and wife comes about through human feeling;
translations.idiomatic: the union of husband and wife comes about through human inclination;

sentences.zh: 君臣之從，以眾心而然者也。

translations.literal: the subordination of minister to ruler comes about through the collective will of the people.
translations.idiomatic: the subjection of minister to ruler comes about through the will of the multitude.

sentences.zh: 是雖欲自廢，而理勢持之，何能斬也。

translations.literal: Even if one wishes to abandon these of oneself, principle and circumstance sustain them — how could they be severed?
translations.idiomatic: Even if one wished to cast them aside, reason and circumstance would uphold them — how could they be cut off?

sentences.zh: 惟朋友者，舉天下之人莫不可同，亦舉天下之人莫不可異，同異在我，則義安所卒歸乎？

translations.literal: Only friendship: among all the people under Heaven, there is none with whom one cannot associate, and likewise none with whom one cannot keep apart. Whether to associate or to part depends on me — then to what end does its principle ultimately return?
translations.idiomatic: Friendship alone is different: of all people under Heaven, there is none with whom one might not become friends, and none with whom one might not remain apart. Since the choice to join or to separate rests with oneself, where does its moral obligation finally settle?

sentences.zh: 是其漸廢之所繇也。

translations.literal: This is the reason friendship has gradually fallen into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: This is why friendship has gradually fallen away.

sentences.zh: 君之於臣也，父之於子也，夫之於婦也，兄之於弟也，過且惡，必亂敗其國家，國家敗而皆受其難，被其名，而終身不可辭也。

translations.literal: When the ruler toward his ministers, the father toward his sons, the husband toward his wife, and the elder brother toward his younger brothers have faults and do evil, they inevitably bring disorder and ruin upon their state and family; when state and family are ruined, all alike suffer calamity, bear the blame, and cannot escape it for a lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: When rulers, fathers, husbands, and elder brothers err and do wrong, they inevitably bring ruin upon their state and household; when state and household collapse, all involved share in the disaster and the disgrace, and none can escape it for life.

sentences.zh: 故其為上者不敢不誨，為下者不敢不諫。

translations.literal: Therefore those above do not dare fail to instruct, and those below do not dare fail to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore those in authority dare not neglect to teach, and those below dare not neglect to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 世治道行，則人能循義而自得；

translations.literal: When the age is governed and the Way is practiced, people can follow duty and thereby find fulfillment on their own;
translations.idiomatic: In an age of good governance and thriving principle, people can follow duty and find satisfaction of their own accord;

sentences.zh: 世衰道微，則人猶顧義而自全。

translations.literal: when the age declines and the Way fades, people still look to duty and thereby preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: in a declining age when principle wanes, people still look to duty and thereby protect themselves.

sentences.zh: 間有不若，則亦無害於眾焉耳。

translations.literal: If occasionally someone falls short, it nevertheless does no harm to the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a few fall short, this does little harm to society at large.

sentences.zh: 此所謂理勢持之，雖百代可知也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by principle and circumstance sustaining these relationships — the pattern can be known even across a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant when we say that reason and circumstance uphold these bonds — the pattern can be seen across a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 親非天性也，合非人情也，從非眾心也，群而同，別而異，有善不足與榮，有惡不足與辱。

translations.literal: Intimacy is not innate disposition; union is not human feeling; subordination is not the will of the multitude. One may gather together or part apart; if one has virtue, it is insufficient to share in glory; if one has vice, it is insufficient to share in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Friendship involves no natural bond, no emotional tie, no collective mandate. Friends may gather or part at will; one man's virtue brings no shared honor, and one man's vice brings no shared shame.

sentences.zh: 大道之行，公與義者可至焉，下斯而言，其能及者鮮矣。

translations.literal: When the Great Way is practiced, those possessing public-mindedness and righteousness can attain it; below this level, those who can reach it are few indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Way prevails, only those of public spirit and righteousness can attain true friendship; below that level, few succeed.

sentences.zh: 是以聖人崇之，以列於君臣、父子、夫婦、兄弟而壹為達道也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages elevated it, listing it alongside ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, and elder and younger brothers as one of the universal relationships.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sages honored it, placing it alongside the other four relationships as one of the universal bonds of society.

sentences.zh: 聖人既沒，而其義益廢，於今則亡矣。

translations.literal: Once the sages had passed away, its principle fell further into disuse, and in the present it is lost altogether.
translations.idiomatic: After the sages died, its principle fell ever more into neglect, until today it has vanished altogether.

sentences.zh: 夫人有四肢，所以成身；

translations.literal: Now, a person has four limbs with which the body is formed;
translations.idiomatic: A human being has four limbs that make up the whole body;

sentences.zh: 一體不備，則謂之廢疾。

translations.literal: if one limb is incomplete, it is called a crippling affliction.
translations.idiomatic: if any one is missing, the person is deemed crippled.

sentences.zh: 而人倫缺焉，何以為世？

translations.literal: Yet human relationships are lacking — how can one exist in the world?
translations.idiomatic: With human relationships incomplete, how can one live in the world?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，處今之時而望古之道，難矣。

translations.literal: Alas, to dwell in the present age and look back to the Way of antiquity — how difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, to live in our age and aspire to the Way of antiquity is no easy thing.

sentences.zh: 姑求其肯告吾過也，而樂聞其過者，與之友乎！

translations.literal: For the present, let us simply seek those willing to tell us of our faults and those who take pleasure in hearing of their faults — shall we befriend them!
translations.idiomatic: For now, let us simply seek out those who will point out our faults and those who welcome having their faults pointed out — let us befriend them!

sentences.zh: 退居潁州，久之不肯仕，在廷多薦者。

translations.literal: He retired to live in Ying Prefecture; for a long time he refused to take office, though many at court recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Ying Prefecture and for a long time declined office, though many at court recommended him.

sentences.zh: 治平中，以為忠武軍節度推官、知南頓縣，命下而卒。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era he was appointed Military Administration Aide of the Zhongwu Army and Prefect of Nandun County, but the order had scarcely been issued when he died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era he was appointed military administration aide of the Zhongwu Army and magistrate of Nandun County, but he died as soon as the appointment was issued.

sentences.zh: 回在潁川，與處士常秩友善。

translations.literal: While Hui was in Yingchuan, he was on friendly terms with the recluse Chang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Yingchuan, Hui was close friends with the recluse Chang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，秩上其文集，補回子汾為郊社齋郎。

translations.literal: During the Xining era, Zhi presented his collected writings to the court, and Hui's son Fen was given the post of Acolyte for Suburban and Altar Sacrifices as compensation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era, Zhi submitted Hui's collected writings to the court, and Hui's son Fen was granted the post of acolyte for suburban and altar sacrifices in recognition.

sentences.zh: 弟向。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 向字子直，為文長於序事，戲作《公默先生傳》曰：

translations.literal: Xiang, courtesy name Zizhi, excelled at narrative exposition in his writings; he playfully composed "A Biography of Mr. Silent," which says:
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, courtesy name Zizhi, was especially skilled at narrative prose. In jest he wrote "A Biography of Mr. Silent," which reads:

sentences.zh: 公議先生剛直任氣，好議論，取當世是非辨明。

translations.literal: Mr. Public Discussion was stern and straight, given to asserting his temperament; he loved to debate and took it upon himself to distinguish right and wrong in current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Public Discussion was stern, upright, and headstrong. He loved debate and made it his business to settle every controversy of the day.

sentences.zh: 遊梁、宋間，不得意。

translations.literal: He traveled between Liang and Song but found no success.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered between Liang and Song but met with no success.

sentences.zh: 去居潁，其徒從者百人。

translations.literal: He left and settled in Ying, with a hundred disciples following him.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on and settled in Ying, followed by a hundred disciples.

sentences.zh: 居二年，與其徒謀，又去潁。

translations.literal: After dwelling there two years, he consulted with his disciples and resolved to leave Ying again.
translations.idiomatic: After two years, he met with his disciples and decided to leave Ying once more.

sentences.zh: 弟子任意對曰：「先生無復念去也，弟子從先生久矣，亦各厭行役。

translations.literal: The disciple Ren Yi replied: "Master, please do not think of leaving again. Your disciples have followed you a long time, and we too are all weary of travel and toil.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Ren Yi replied, "Master, please put leaving out of your mind. We have followed you for a long time, and we too are weary of wandering.

sentences.zh: 先生舍潁為居廬，少有生計。

translations.literal: The master gave up Ying to make a dwelling here; we have some modest means of livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: You made a home in Ying and left your former dwelling; we have a modest livelihood here.

sentences.zh: 主人公賢，遇先生不淺薄，今又去之，弟子未見先生止處也。

translations.literal: Our host is a worthy man and has treated the master with no meagerness; if you leave again now, your disciples see no place where the master might finally settle.
translations.idiomatic: Our host is a worthy man who has treated you generously. If you leave again, we cannot see where you will ever find rest.

sentences.zh: 先生豈薄潁邪？」

translations.literal: Could the master perhaps be looking down on Ying?"
translations.idiomatic: Has the master perhaps come to despise Ying?"

sentences.zh: 公議先生曰：「來，吾語爾！

translations.literal: Mr. Public Discussion said: "Come here — let me tell you!
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Public Discussion said, "Come here — let me explain.

sentences.zh: 君子貴行道信於世，不信貴容，不容貴去，古之辟世、辟地、辟色、辟言是也。

translations.literal: The gentleman values practicing the Way and winning trust in the world; if trust is lacking, he values forbearance; if forbearance is lacking, he values departure — such were the ancient practices of withdrawing from the age, from the land, from distasteful countenance, and from perilous speech.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman prizes practicing the Way and earning the world's trust. If he cannot, he prizes tolerance. If he cannot tolerate his situation, he prizes departure — as in the ancient practices of withdrawing from troubled times, from hostile places, from offensive company, and from dangerous speech.

sentences.zh: 吾行年三十，立節循名，被服先王，究窮《六經》。

translations.literal: I am now thirty years of age; I established my principles and pursued my reputation, dressed myself in the ways of the former kings, and exhaustively studied the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: I am thirty years old. I have set my principles and guarded my reputation, clothed myself in the ways of the ancient kings, and mastered the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 頑鈍晚成，所得無幾。

translations.literal: Slow of wit and late in maturing, I have gained but little.
translations.idiomatic: Dull by nature and slow to mature, I have achieved little.

sentences.zh: 張羅大綱，漏略零細。

translations.literal: I spread a wide net with large meshes and let slip the fine details.
translations.idiomatic: I cast a broad net and let finer points slip through.

sentences.zh: 校其所見，未為完人。

translations.literal: Weighing what I know, I am not yet a complete man.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by what I know, I am no perfected man.

sentences.zh: 豈敢自忘，冀用於世？

translations.literal: How dare I forget myself? Yet I still hope to be employed by the world.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not abandon my principles — and yet I still hope to serve the world.

sentences.zh: 予所厭苦，正謂不容。

translations.literal: What I find bitter and wearisome is precisely this lack of tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: What grieves me is precisely that I am not tolerated.

sentences.zh: 予行世間，波混流同。

translations.literal: As I move through the world, waves mingle and currents run together.
translations.idiomatic: As I move through the world, every wave blends and every current runs alike.

sentences.zh: 予譽不至，予毀日隆。

translations.literal: My praise does not reach me, while my slander grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: Praise never reaches me, but slander mounts day by day.

sentences.zh: 小人鑿空，造事形跡；

translations.literal: Petty men bore holes in the void and fabricate outward traces of deeds;
translations.idiomatic: Petty men invent falsehoods from nothing and manufacture incriminating evidence;

sentences.zh: 侵排萬端，地隘天側。

translations.literal: their encroachments and plots are myriad; the ground grows narrow and the sky turns sideways.
translations.idiomatic: their schemes assail me from every side until the ground narrows beneath me and the sky itself seems to tilt.

sentences.zh: 《詩》不云乎，『讒人罔極』。

translations.literal: Does not the Book of Poetry say, "The slanderer knows no limit"?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Book of Poetry say, "Slanderers know no bounds"?

sentences.zh: 主人明恕，故未見疑。

translations.literal: Our host is clear-sighted and forgiving, and therefore has not yet grown suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Our host is wise and forgiving, so he has not yet grown suspicious.

sentences.zh: 不幸去我，來者謂誰？

translations.literal: If by misfortune he should leave us, who would come after?
translations.idiomatic: If by ill luck he should be gone, who would take his place?

sentences.zh: 讒一日效，我終顛危。

translations.literal: Once slander takes effect for a single day, I will ultimately topple into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The moment slander succeeds, I will be brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 智者利身，遠害全德，不如亟行，以適異國。」

translations.literal: The wise man benefits his person, keeps distant from harm, and preserves his virtue intact — better to depart at once and go to a foreign land."
translations.idiomatic: The wise protect themselves, flee harm, and preserve their virtue whole. Better to leave at once for a distant land."

sentences.zh: 語已，任意對曰：「先生無言也。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, Ren Yi replied: "Master, say no more.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, Ren Yi replied, "Master, say no more.

sentences.zh: 意輩弟子嘗竊論先生樂取怨憎，為人所難，不知不樂也。

translations.literal: We disciples once privately discussed whether the master took pleasure in inviting resentment and hatred — doing what others find difficult — unaware that you take no pleasure in it.
translations.idiomatic: We disciples once wondered privately whether you took pleasure in inviting hatred by doing what others find impossible. We did not realize that you take no pleasure in it.

sentences.zh: 今定不樂，先生知所以取之乎？

translations.literal: Now we know for certain that you take no pleasure in it — does the master know the reason you invite it?
translations.idiomatic: Now we know you take no pleasure in it. Does the master understand why he keeps inviting it?

sentences.zh: 先生聰明才能，過人遠甚，而刺口論世事，立是立非，其間不容毫髮。

translations.literal: The master's intelligence and talent far surpass those of others, yet you are sharp-tongued in debating affairs of the day, establishing right and wrong with not a hair's breadth of tolerance between them.
translations.idiomatic: Your intelligence and talent far exceed those of ordinary men, yet you are sharp-tongued in judging affairs of the day, pronouncing right and wrong with not a hair's breadth of compromise.

sentences.zh: 又以公議名，此人之怨府也。

translations.literal: Moreover you bear the name Public Discussion — this is a storehouse of human resentment.
translations.idiomatic: And you bear the name Public Discussion — a title that makes you a magnet for resentment.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『議人者不得其死』，先生憂之是也，其去未是。

translations.literal: The Commentary says, "One who freely judges others does not die a natural death." The master's worry is justified, but departure is not the right course.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, "Those who freely criticize others do not die natural deaths." Your worry is justified, but leaving is not the answer.

sentences.zh: 意有三事為先生計，先生幸聽意，不必行；

translations.literal: Yi has three plans to propose for the master; I hope the master will hear me out — you need not leave;
translations.idiomatic: I have three strategies to propose. I hope you will hear me out — there is no need to leave;

sentences.zh: 不聽，先生雖去絕海，未見先生安也。」

translations.literal: if you will not listen, even if the master goes to the ends of the sea, I see no peace for you."
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse to listen, even if you flee to the ends of the earth, I do not see how you will find peace."

sentences.zh: 公議先生強舌不語，下視任意，目不轉移時，卒問任意，對曰：「人之肺肝，安得可視，高出重泉，險不足比。

translations.literal: Mr. Public Discussion held his tongue and said nothing, looking down at Ren Yi without shifting his gaze for a time; finally he asked Ren Yi, who replied: "The innermost hearts and livers of men — how can they be seen? They stand deeper than the lowest spring and are more treacherous than anything below comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Public Discussion clamped his tongue and said nothing, staring down at Ren Yi without shifting his eyes. At last he asked him to speak. Ren Yi replied, "Who can see into the secret hearts of men? They lie deeper than the lowest spring and are more treacherous than any abyss.

sentences.zh: 聞善於彼，陽譽陰非，反背復憎，詆笑縱橫。

translations.literal: When they hear of another's virtue, they praise openly but disapprove in secret; they turn their backs, then hate again; slander and mockery fly in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: When they hear that someone else is good, they praise him to his face but condemn him behind his back. They turn away, then despise him anew. Slander and ridicule fly in every direction.

sentences.zh: 得其細過，聲張口播，緣飾百端，得敗行破。

translations.literal: Once they grasp a minor fault, they spread it with loud voice and open mouth, embellishing it in a hundred ways until reputation is ruined and conduct destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Seize the smallest fault and they broadcast it at the top of their lungs, dressing it up every which way until reputation and character alike are destroyed.

sentences.zh: 自然是人，賤彼善我。

translations.literal: By nature this is how people are — they despise the good in others and favor themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Such is human nature: we despise others' virtues and exalt our own.

sentences.zh: 意策之三，此為最上者也。

translations.literal: Of the three strategies Yi proposes, this is the highest.
translations.idiomatic: Of my three strategies, this is the highest.

sentences.zh: 先生能用之乎？」

translations.literal: Can the master employ it?
translations.idiomatic: Can you adopt it?

sentences.zh: 公議先生曰：「不能，爾試言其次者。」

translations.literal: Mr. Public Discussion said: "I cannot. Try telling me the next one.
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Public Discussion said, "I cannot. Tell me the next strategy.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「捐棄骨肉，佯狂而去，令世人不復顧忌。

translations.literal: Ren Yi replied: "Abandon flesh and bone relations, feign madness, and depart — so that the people of the world no longer need concern themselves about you.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yi replied, "Abandon your family, feign madness, and wander off so that the world no longer pays you any heed.

sentences.zh: 此策之次者，先生能用之乎？」

translations.literal: This is the second strategy — can the master employ it?
translations.idiomatic: This is the second strategy. Can you adopt it?

sentences.zh: 公議先生曰：「不能，爾試言其又次者。」

translations.literal: Mr. Public Discussion said: "I cannot. Try telling me the one after that.
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Public Discussion said, "I cannot. Tell me the one below that.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「先生之行己，視世人所不逮何等也！

translations.literal: Ren Yi replied: "In the master's conduct toward yourself, how far do you surpass what the people of the world cannot reach!
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yi replied, "In your personal conduct, how far you surpass what ordinary men can achieve!

sentences.zh: 曾未得稱高世，而詆訶鋒起，幾不得與妄庸人伍者，良以口禍也。

translations.literal: Yet you have not yet been called a man towering above the age, while denunciation and abuse surge like blades — you can scarcely be ranked with reckless mediocrities; the real cause is calamity brought by the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have not even been hailed as a man above the age, while abuse swirls around you and you can scarcely keep company with ordinary fools — all because of the disaster wrought by your tongue.

sentences.zh: 先生能不好議而好默，是非不及口而心存焉，何疾於不容？

translations.literal: If the master could love silence rather than debate — keeping right and wrong from passing the lips while holding them in the heart — what would prevent tolerance?
translations.idiomatic: If you could prefer silence to debate — keeping judgment in your heart rather than on your tongue — what would keep the world from accepting you?

sentences.zh: 此策之最下者也，先生能用之乎？」

translations.literal: This is the lowest of the three strategies — can the master employ it?
translations.idiomatic: This is the lowest of the three strategies. Can you adopt it?

sentences.zh: 公議先生喟然歎曰：「籲，吾為爾用下策也。」

translations.literal: Mr. Public Discussion sighed deeply and said: "Alas! I will adopt your lowest strategy for you."
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Public Discussion sighed and said, "Alas — I will take your lowest strategy."

sentences.zh: 任意乃大笑，顧其徒曰：「宜吾先生之病於世也。

translations.literal: Ren Yi then laughed loudly and, turning to the disciples, said: "No wonder our master suffers illness in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yi laughed aloud and said to the disciples, "No wonder our master is ill at ease in the world.

sentences.zh: 吾三策之，卒取其下者矣。」

translations.literal: I offered him three strategies, and in the end he took the lowest.
translations.idiomatic: I gave him three strategies, and he chose the lowest.

sentences.zh: 弟子陽思曰：「今日非任意，先生不可得留。」

translations.literal: The disciple Yang Si said: "If not for Ren Yi today, the master could not have been kept here.
translations.idiomatic: The disciple Yang Si said, "If not for Ren Yi today, the master could never have been persuaded to stay.

sentences.zh: 與其徒謝意，更因意請，去公議為公默先生。

translations.literal: He and his disciples thanked Yi and, further acting on Yi's request, changed Public Discussion to Mr. Silent.
translations.idiomatic: He and his disciples thanked Ren Yi and, at his urging, changed the master's name from Public Discussion to Mr. Silent.

sentences.zh: 弟同，字容季。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Tong, courtesy name Rongji.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Tong, courtesy name Rongji.

sentences.zh: 性純篤，亦善序事。

translations.literal: In nature he was pure and sincere, and he too was skilled at narrative exposition.
translations.idiomatic: He was sincere and steadfast by nature and was also skilled at narrative prose.

sentences.zh: 皆早卒。

translations.literal: All died young.
translations.idiomatic: All three brothers died young.

sentences.zh: 仕止於縣主簿。

translations.literal: Their official service stopped at County Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Their official careers ended at the rank of county recorder.

sentences.zh: 周堯卿，字子俞，道州永明人。

translations.literal: Zhou Yaoqing, courtesy name Ziyu, was a man of Yongming in Dao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yaoqing, courtesy name Ziyu, was a native of Yongming in Dao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 警悟強記，以學行知名。

translations.literal: He was sharp-witted with a powerful memory, and was renowned for his learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and possessing a powerful memory, he was renowned for scholarship and personal integrity.

sentences.zh: 天聖二年舉進士，曆連、衡二州司理參軍、桂州司錄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng he passed the jinshi examination and served successively as judicial assistant in Lian and Heng Prefectures and registrar in Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Tiansheng era and served successively as judicial assistant in Lian and Heng prefectures and as registrar in Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知高安、寧化二縣，提點刑獄紘入境，有被刑而耘苗者，紘就詢其故，對曰：「貧以利故，為人直其枉，令不我欺而我欺之，我又何怨？」

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Gao'an and Ninghua counties. When Hong, the circuit intendant for criminal justice, entered the territory, he encountered someone bearing the marks of punishment while hoeing seedlings. Hong went up and asked the reason. The man replied: "Out of poverty and for profit's sake, I straightened another man's injustice for him. The magistrate did not deceive me, yet I deceived him — so what grievance have I?"
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Gao'an and Ninghua counties. When Hong, the circuit intendant for criminal justice, entered the district, he saw a man bearing the marks of punishment while hoeing in the fields. Hong went over and asked why. The man replied, "Poor as I am, I took money to right another man's wrong. The magistrate never deceived me, but I deceived him — so what right have I to complain?"

sentences.zh: 紘至縣，以所聞薦之。

translations.literal: When Hong reached the county seat, he recommended Yaoqing based on what he had heard.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong reached the county seat, he recommended Yaoqing on the strength of what he had heard.

sentences.zh: 後通判饒州，積官至太常博士。

translations.literal: Later he served as administrative assistant of Rao Prefecture and, by accumulated offices, reached Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as administrative assistant of Rao Prefecture and eventually rose to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹薦經行可為師表，未及用，以慶曆五年卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan recommended his classical learning and conduct as worthy of serving as a teacher's model; before he could be employed, he died in the fifth year of Qingli at the age of fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan recommended him as a model of scholarship and conduct, but before he could be appointed he died in the fifth year of the Qingli era at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 始，堯卿年十二喪父，憂戚如成人，見母則抑情忍哀，不欲傷其意。

translations.literal: At the beginning — when Yaoqing was twelve and lost his father — he grieved as an adult would; when he saw his mother he suppressed his feelings and restrained his sorrow, not wishing to wound her heart.
