translations.idiomatic: When Yaoqing was twelve and lost his father, he grieved as deeply as a grown man. In his mother's presence he restrained his sorrow so as not to add to her grief.

sentences.zh: 母知而異之，謂族人曰：「是兒愛我如此，多知孝養矣。」

translations.literal: His mother learned of this and marveled at it, saying to the clan: "This child loves me thus — he already understands much of filial nurture.
translations.idiomatic: His mother noticed and was moved, and she said to the clan, "This child loves me so deeply — he already understands a great deal about filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 卒能如母之言。

translations.literal: In the end he was able to do as his mother had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he lived up to his mother's words.

sentences.zh: 及母喪，倚廬三年，席薪枕塊，雖疾病，不飲酒食肉。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he lived in a mourning hut for three years, sleeping on firewood and using a clod for a pillow; even when ill, he did not drink wine or eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he lived in a mourning hut for three years, sleeping on firewood and using a clod for a pillow; even when ill, he abstained from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 既葬，慈烏百數銜土集隴上，人以為孝感所致。

translations.literal: After the burial, several hundred benevolent crows carried earth and gathered it on the mound; people believed this was caused by filial feeling moving heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, several hundred crows carried earth and gathered it on the mound; people believed this was caused by filial devotion moving heaven.

sentences.zh: 其於昆弟尤篤友愛。

translations.literal: Toward his brothers he was especially devoted and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: Toward his brothers he was especially devoted and affectionate.

sentences.zh: 又為人簡重不校，有慢己者，必厚為禮以愧之。

translations.literal: He was also by nature dignified and uncontentious; when someone slighted him, he always treated them with generous courtesy to shame them.
translations.idiomatic: He was also by nature dignified and uncontentious; when someone slighted him, he always treated them with generous courtesy to shame them into better conduct.

sentences.zh: 居官祿雖薄，必以周宗族朋友，罄而後已。

translations.literal: Though his official salary was meager, he always used it to support clan and friends, not stopping until it was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Though his official salary was meager, he always used it to support clan and friends, not stopping until it was exhausted.

sentences.zh: 為學不專於傳注，問辨思索，以通為期。

translations.literal: In learning he did not limit himself to commentaries; through questioning, debate, and reflection, he aimed at comprehensive understanding.
translations.idiomatic: In his studies he did not limit himself to commentaries; through questioning, debate, and reflection, he aimed at comprehensive understanding.

sentences.zh: 長於毛、鄭《詩》及《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He excelled in the Mao and Zheng commentaries on the Odes and in Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in the Mao and Zheng commentaries on the Odes and in Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 其學《詩》，以孔子所謂「《詩》三百，一言以蔽之曰：『思無邪』」，孟子所謂「說《詩》者以意逆誌，是為得之」，考經指歸，而見毛、鄭之得失。

translations.literal: In studying the Odes, he took Confucius's saying that "the three hundred Odes can be summed up in one phrase: 'Have no devious thoughts'" and Mencius's saying that "one who explains the Odes uses intent to meet the author's purpose—this is obtaining it," examined the classic's essential meaning, and thereby saw the strengths and weaknesses of Mao and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In studying the Odes, he took Confucius's saying that "the three hundred Odes can be summed up in one phrase: 'Have no devious thoughts'" and Mencius's saying that "one who explains the Odes uses intent to meet the author's purpose—this is obtaining it," examined the classic's essential meaning, and thereby discerned the strengths and weaknesses of Mao and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 曰：「毛之傳欲簡，或寡於義理，非一言以蔽之也。

translations.literal: He said, "Mao's commentary aims at brevity and sometimes lacks in principle and reason—it cannot be summed up in a single phrase.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Mao's commentary aims at brevity and sometimes lacks in principle and reason—it cannot be summed up in a single phrase.

sentences.zh: 鄭之箋欲詳，或遠於性情，非以意逆誌也。

translations.literal: Zheng's subcommentary aims at detail and sometimes departs from human feeling and nature—it is not using intent to meet the author's purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's subcommentary aims at detail and sometimes departs from human feeling and nature—it is not using intent to meet the author's purpose.

sentences.zh: 是可以無去取乎？」

translations.literal: Can one then do without choosing and rejecting?"
translations.idiomatic: Can one then do without choosing and rejecting between them?"

sentences.zh: 其學《春秋》，由左氏記之詳，得經之所以書者，至《三傳》之異同，均有所不取。

translations.literal: In studying Spring and Autumn Annals, through the detail of Mr. Zuo's record he obtained why the classic was written as it was; as for the differences among the Three Commentaries, he rejected portions of all alike.
translations.idiomatic: In studying the Spring and Autumn Annals, through the detail of Mr. Zuo's record he grasped why the classic was written as it was; as for the differences among the Three Commentaries, he rejected portions of all alike.

sentences.zh: 曰：「聖人之意豈二致耶？」

translations.literal: He said, "Could the sage's intent be twofold?"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Could the sage's intent be twofold?"

sentences.zh: 讀莊周、孟子之書，曰：「周善言理，未至於窮理。

translations.literal: Reading the books of Zhuang Zhou and Mencius, he said, "Zhou is good at speaking of principle but has not reached the exhaustion of principle.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the books of Zhuang Zhou and Mencius, he said, "Zhou is good at speaking of principle but has not reached the full exhaustion of principle.

sentences.zh: 窮理，則好惡不繆於聖人，孟軻是已。

translations.literal: To exhaust principle is for likes and dislikes not to stray from the sage—Meng Ke is such a one.
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust principle is for likes and dislikes not to stray from the sage—Mencius is such a one.

sentences.zh: 孟善言性，未至於盡己之性。

translations.literal: Meng is good at speaking of nature but has not reached the exhaustion of one's own nature.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius is good at speaking of nature but has not reached the full exhaustion of one's own nature.

sentences.zh: 能盡己之性，則能盡物之性，而可與天地參，其唯聖人乎。

translations.literal: One who can exhaust one's own nature can exhaust the nature of things and participate with heaven and earth—only the sage can do this.
translations.idiomatic: One who can fully exhaust one's own nature can exhaust the nature of things and participate with heaven and earth—only the sage can do this.

sentences.zh: 天何言哉？

translations.literal: What does Heaven say?
translations.idiomatic: What does Heaven say?

sentences.zh: 性與天道，子貢所以不可得而聞也。

translations.literal: Nature and the Way of Heaven are what Zigong could not obtain and hear.
translations.idiomatic: Nature and the Way of Heaven are what Zigong could not obtain and hear.

sentences.zh: 昔宰我、子貢善為說辭，冉牛、閔子、顏淵善言德行，孔子曰：『我於辭命，則不能也。』

translations.literal: Formerly Zai Wo and Zigong were skilled at rhetoric; Ran Niu, Min Zi, and Yan Yuan were skilled at speaking of virtue and conduct. Confucius said, "As for rhetoric, I cannot do it."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zai Wo and Zigong were skilled at rhetoric; Ran Niu, Min Zi, and Yan Yuan were skilled at speaking of virtue and conduct. Confucius said, "As for rhetoric, I cannot do it."

sentences.zh: 惟不言，故曰不能而已，蓋言生於不足者也。」

translations.literal: Only because he did not speak did he say he could not—that is all. Speech arises from insufficiency."
translations.idiomatic: Only because he did not speak did he say he could not—that is all. Speech arises from insufficiency."

sentences.zh: 其講解議論皆若是。

translations.literal: His lectures and discussions were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His lectures and discussions were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 有《詩》、《春秋說》各三十卷，文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had thirty chapters each of Expositions on the Odes and Expositions on Spring and Autumn Annals, and twenty chapters of collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: He authored thirty chapters each of Expositions on the Odes and Expositions on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and twenty chapters of collected writings.

sentences.zh: 七子：諭，鼎州司理參軍；

translations.literal: Seven sons: Yu, Judicial Officer of Ding Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Yu, Judicial Officer of Ding Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 詵，湖州歸安主簿；

translations.literal: Shen, Clerk of Gui'an in Hu Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Shen, clerk of Gui'an in Hu Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 謐、諷、諲、說、誼。

translations.literal: Mi, Feng, Yin, Shuo, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, Feng, Yin, Shuo, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 王當，字子思，眉州眉山人。

translations.literal: Wang Dang, courtesy name Zisi, was a man of Meishan in Mei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dang, courtesy name Zisi, was a native of Meishan in Mei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，博覽古今，所取惟王佐大略。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; he broadly read ancient and modern works, taking only the great outlines of statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning; he broadly read ancient and modern works, taking only the great outlines of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂三公論道經邦，燮理陰陽，填撫四方，親附百姓，皆出於一道，其言之雖大，其行之甚易。

translations.literal: He once said that the Three Excellencies discuss the Way and govern the state, harmonize yin and yang, pacify the four directions, and draw the people close—all spring from one Way; though the words are grand, the practice is very easy.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that the Three Excellencies discuss the Way and govern the state, harmonize yin and yang, pacify the four directions, and draw the people close—all spring from one Way; though the words are grand, the practice is very easy.

sentences.zh: 嘗舉進士不中，退居田野，歎曰：「士之居世，苟不見其用，必見其言。」

translations.literal: He once failed the jinshi examination, retired to the countryside, and sighed, "When a scholar lives in the world, if he is not seen in use, he must be seen in his words."
translations.idiomatic: He once failed the jinshi examination, retired to the countryside, and sighed, "When a scholar lives in the world, if he is not seen in use, he must be seen in his words."

sentences.zh: 遂著《春秋列國名臣傳》五十卷，人競傳之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he authored fifty chapters of Biographies of Famous Ministers of the Spring and Autumn States, which people competed to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he authored fifty chapters of Biographies of Famous Ministers of the Spring and Autumn States, which people competed to circulate.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，蘇轍以賢良方正薦。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou, Su Zhe recommended him as Worthy and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou, Su Zhe recommended him as Worthy and Upright.

sentences.zh: 廷對慷慨，不避權貴，策入四等。

translations.literal: In the palace examination he spoke boldly and did not avoid the powerful; his policy essay placed in the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination he spoke boldly and did not avoid the powerful; his policy essay placed in the fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 調龍遊縣尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as Magistrate of Longyou County.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as magistrate of Longyou County.

sentences.zh: 蔡京知成都，舉為學官，當不就。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing was Prefect of Chengdu, he recommended Dang as instructor, but Dang did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing was Prefect of Chengdu, he recommended Dang as instructor, but Dang did not accept.

sentences.zh: 其後京相，當遂不復仕，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: Afterward, when Jing became chancellor, Dang never again took office; he died at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, when Jing became chancellor, Dang never again took office; he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 當於經學尤邃《易》與《春秋》，皆為之傳，得聖人之旨居多。

translations.literal: Dang was especially deep in classical learning in the Changes and Spring and Autumn Annals; he wrote commentaries on both, mostly obtaining the sage's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Dang was especially deep in classical learning in the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals; he wrote commentaries on both, mostly obtaining the sage's intent.

sentences.zh: 又有《經旨》三卷，《史論》十二卷，《兵書》十二篇。

translations.literal: He also had three chapters of Essential Meaning of the Classics, twelve chapters of Historical Discussions, and twelve chapters on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also authored three chapters of Essential Meaning of the Classics, twelve chapters of Historical Discussions, and twelve chapters on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 陳暘字晉之，福州人。

translations.literal: Chen Yang, courtesy name Jinzhi, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yang, courtesy name Jinzhi, was a native of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 中紹聖製科，授順昌軍節度推官。

translations.literal: He passed the Shaosheng special examination and was appointed Military Commissioner Staff Officer of Shunchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Shaosheng special examination and was appointed Military Commissioner Staff Officer of Shunchang Army.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，進《迓衡集》以勸導紹述，得太學博士、秘書省正字。

translations.literal: In the early Huizong era he submitted the Collection on Welcoming Balance to encourage continuation of the reform policies, and was appointed Doctor of the Imperial Academy and Proofreader of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Huizong era he submitted the Collection on Welcoming Balance to encourage continuation of the reform policies, and was appointed Doctor of the Imperial Academy and Proofreader of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎趙挺之言，暘所著《樂書》二十卷貫穿明備，乞援其兄祥道進《禮書》故事給劄。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Zhao Tingzhi said that Yang's Book of Music in twenty chapters was comprehensive and complete, and requested following the precedent of his elder brother Xiangdao's submission of the Book of Rites to grant an appointment letter.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Zhao Tingzhi said that Yang's Book of Music in twenty chapters was comprehensive and complete, and requested following the precedent of his elder brother Xiangdao's submission of the Book of Rites to grant an appointment letter.

sentences.zh: 既上，遷太常丞，進駕部員外郎，為講議司參詳禮樂官。

translations.literal: After submission he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Transport, and made an officer of the Discussion Bureau for examining rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: After submission he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Transport, and made an officer of the Discussion Bureau for examining rites and music.

sentences.zh: 魏漢津議樂，用京房二變四清。

translations.literal: Wei Hanjin proposed music using Jing Fang's two mutations and four clear tones.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hanjin proposed music using Jing Fang's two mutations and four clear tones.

sentences.zh: 暘曰：「五聲十二律，樂之正也。

translations.literal: Yang said, "The five tones and twelve pitch pipes are the orthodox in music.
translations.idiomatic: Yang said, "The five tones and twelve pitch pipes are the orthodox in music.

sentences.zh: 二變四清，樂之蠹也。

translations.literal: The two mutations and four clear tones are pests in music.
translations.idiomatic: The two mutations and four clear tones are pests in music.

sentences.zh: 二變以變宮為君，四清以黃鍾清為君。

translations.literal: The two mutations take the mutated palace tone as sovereign; the four clear tones take the clear yellow bell as sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: The two mutations take the mutated palace tone as sovereign; the four clear tones take the clear yellow bell as sovereign.

sentences.zh: 事以時作，固可變也，而君不可變。

translations.literal: Affairs may be performed according to the season and thus may change, but the sovereign cannot change.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs may be performed according to the season and thus may change, but the sovereign cannot change.

sentences.zh: 太簇、大呂、夾鍾，或可分也，而黃鍾不可分。

translations.literal: Great cluster, great pitch-pipe, and compressed bell may perhaps be divided, but the yellow bell cannot be divided.
translations.idiomatic: Great cluster, great pitch-pipe, and compressed bell may perhaps be divided, but the yellow bell cannot be divided.

sentences.zh: 豈古人所謂尊無二上之旨哉？」

translations.literal: Is this not the ancient meaning that in honor there is no second above?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this not the ancient meaning that in honor there is no second above?"

sentences.zh: 時論方右漢津，絀暘議。

translations.literal: At the time opinion favored Hanjin, and Yang's proposal was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: At the time opinion favored Hanjin, and Yang's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 進鴻臚太常少卿、禮部侍郎，以顯謨閣待制提舉醴泉觀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Minister of Rites, and as Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Manifest Counsel was appointed Director of the Sweet Spring Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Vice Minister of Rites, and as Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Manifest Counsel was appointed Director of the Sweet Spring Abbey.

sentences.zh: 嘗坐事奪，已而復之。

translations.literal: He was once stripped of rank for an offense, but later restored.
translations.idiomatic: He was once stripped of rank for an offense, but later restored.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 祥道字用之。

translations.literal: Xiangdao, courtesy name Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangdao, courtesy name Yongzhi.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，為太常博士，終秘書省正字。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou he was Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and ended as Proofreader of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou he served as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and ended his career as Proofreader of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 所著《禮書》一百五十卷，與暘《樂書》並行於世。

translations.literal: His Book of Rites in one hundred fifty chapters circulated in the world together with Yang's Book of Music.
translations.idiomatic: His Book of Rites in one hundred fifty chapters circulated in the world together with Yang's Book of Music.
